senses.title: A deep round container for cooking or storing
senses.definition: a deep round vessel, usually with a lid, used for cooking food or keeping things in
senses.definitionCN: 通常带盖的深圆容器，用来做饭或存放东西
senses.example: She left the soup simmering in a heavy iron pot.
senses.exampleCN: 她把汤留在一口厚重的铁锅里慢慢炖着。
senses.why: Old English pott named a rounded vessel before it named any particular use, so cooking is only one of the jobs the container was given.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 pott 先指一种圆鼓鼓的容器，并不限定用途，做饭只是人们后来交给它的活儿之一。

senses.title: The amount a pot holds
senses.definition: as much as a pot contains, used as a rough measure in cooking and serving
senses.definitionCN: 一锅或一罐所装的分量，在烹饪与待客时用作粗略的计量
senses.example: He made a pot of coffee for the four of them.
senses.exampleCN: 他煮了一壶咖啡给四个人喝。
senses.why: A container word slides to its contents because the two are always seen together, and English lets pot measure coffee or soup without any extra suffix.
senses.whyCN: 容器和里面的东西总是一起出现，于是容器词顺势指内容物；英语不必加后缀，pot 就能直接量咖啡或汤。

senses.title: A container for a growing plant
senses.definition: a round container filled with soil in which a plant is grown indoors or on a windowsill
senses.definitionCN: 装满泥土、在室内或窗台上种花的圆形容器
senses.example: The basil on the windowsill needs a bigger pot.
senses.exampleCN: 窗台上的罗勒需要换一个更大的花盆。
senses.why: When clay vessels were stood in gardens and on windowsills, the same word that named a kitchen vessel came to name the vessel a plant lives in.
senses.whyCN: 当陶制容器被摆到院子里和窗台上，原本指厨房器皿的词就转而指植物所住的容器。

senses.title: To plant something in a pot
senses.definition: to put a plant into a container filled with soil so that it can grow there
senses.definitionCN: 把植物放进装了土的容器里，让它在其中生长
senses.example: She potted the young tomato plants before the first frost.
senses.exampleCN: 初霜之前，她把番茄苗移栽进了盆里。
senses.why: English turns nouns into verbs without adding anything, so the name of the container became the name of the act of putting a plant into it.
senses.whyCN: 英语可以不添任何成分就把名词用作动词，于是容器的名字变成了「把植物放进容器」这个动作的名字。

senses.title: The money staked in a card game
senses.definition: the total amount of money that players have put into the middle of the table in a game of cards
senses.definitionCN: 牌局中玩家押到桌面中央的钱的总数
senses.example: By the last hand there was a small fortune in the pot.
senses.exampleCN: 到最后一局时，桌上的赌注已经是一笔不小的钱。
senses.why: Card players drop their stakes into a central dish, and English simply moved the name of that dish onto the money it held, keeping the picture of a shared vessel.
senses.whyCN: 牌手把赌注丢进桌子中央的盘子里，英语直接把盘子的名字挪到里面的钱上，共用一只容器的画面留了下来。

intro.en: Pot is an old Germanic vessel word. Whether it was lent to Latin or borrowed from Latin is still argued, so the deeper origin is usually given with a hedge.
intro.cn: pot 是一个古老的日耳曼语容器词。它究竟是借给了拉丁语，还是从拉丁语借来，至今仍有争论，所以更远的来历通常要加一句「一般认为」。

items.en: A reconstructed Germanic word for a rounded vessel; the asterisk marks a form rebuilt by comparing later languages, not one found written down.
items.cn: 这是为「圆形容器」重构出来的日耳曼语词；星号表示它是靠比较后世语言推出来的，并非有文字记录的形式。

items.en: Old English pott names a deep vessel, and this is the form English has kept to the present day.
items.cn: 古英语 pott 指深腹容器，英语一直把这个形式保留到今天。

items.en: Many dictionaries think the Germanic word was borrowed from a Vulgar Latin pottus for a drinking vessel, but the direction of the borrowing is not settled.
items.cn: 不少词典认为这个日耳曼词借自俗拉丁语 pottus（饮器），但借用的方向至今没有定论。

items.en: If the vessel word does go back to Latin, its ultimate root is potare, to drink, with potio, a drink, beside it.
items.cn: 如果这个容器词确实可追溯到拉丁语，它更远的根就是 potare（饮），旁边的 potio 意为饮料。

items.en: Modern English extended the vessel to flower pots, to the stakes in a card game, and to the verb of planting.
items.cn: 现代英语把这件容器扩展到花盆、牌桌上的赌注，还把它用作「栽种」的动词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the vessel itself; the near-meaning group gathers other kitchen and table containers.
note.cn: 形近组收直接由这件容器构成的词；近义组收厨房与餐桌上其他容器词。

normalIntro.en: The word has named a round vessel for over a thousand years, and most of its other uses are that vessel seen from a different angle.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词指一种圆容器已有一千多年，它其余的用法大多只是从不同角度去看这件容器。

normal.en: Old English pott already meant a deep vessel, so the word is older than any recipe written in English.
normal.cn: 古英语 pott 已经是「深容器」的意思，所以这个词比任何英语写成的菜谱都老。

normal.en: Add -ful and the vessel becomes a measure: a potful is as much as it takes to fill one.
normal.cn: 加上 -ful，容器就变成量词：potful 就是装满一只锅的分量。

normal.en: Add -er and you get the person, potter, the one who makes the vessel.
normal.cn: 加上 -er 就得到人：potter 是做这件容器的人。

normal.en: Add -ery and you get the craft and its place: pottery is both the ware and the workshop.
normal.cn: 加上 -ery 就得到手艺与场所：pottery 既指陶器，也指陶艺作坊。

normal.en: Pot luck and go to pot keep the old household picture: whatever the pot happens to hold, or a house gone to ruin.
normal.cn: pot luck 与 go to pot 都留着旧日居家的画面：锅里碰巧有什么，或者一个家败落下去。

abstract.en: A pot is defined by what it can hold, so the word slides easily from vessel to contents to the money on a table.
abstract.cn: 锅由它能装什么来定义，所以这个词很自然地从事物滑到内容，再滑到桌上的钱。

abstract.en: Round, deep and lidded: the shape is the meaning, and every new use keeps that shape somewhere in view.
abstract.cn: 圆、深、有盖：形状本身就是词义，每个新用法都在某处保留着这个形状。

abstract.en: The same word feeds a kitchen, a garden and a card table, because all three need something to put things into.
abstract.cn: 同一个词同时养活厨房、花园和牌桌，因为这三处都需要一个能装东西的容器。

senses.title: The British unit of money
senses.definition: the standard unit of money in Britain, divided into one hundred pence
senses.definitionCN: 英国的标准货币单位，一英镑分为一百便士
senses.example: The ticket cost twenty pounds, which was more than he expected.
senses.exampleCN: 这张票要二十英镑，比他预想的多。
senses.why: English took the name of a weight for silver and used it for the money made of that weight, so the currency still carries a scale inside its name.
senses.whyCN: 英语把称银子用的重量名直接拿来指那个重量的银子所铸的钱，所以这种货币的名字里至今藏着一杆秤。

senses.title: A unit of weight
senses.definition: a unit of weight equal to about 454 grams, used in Britain and the United States
senses.definitionCN: 约合四百五十四克的重量单位，通行于英国与美国
senses.example: The recipe asks for two pounds of potatoes.
senses.exampleCN: 这份食谱要两磅土豆。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense in English: Old English pund weighed goods at the market long before it counted coins at the bank.
senses.whyCN: 这是英语里最老的义项：古英语 pund 早在银行数钱之前，就已经在市场上称货物了。

senses.title: To strike something hard and repeatedly
senses.definition: to hit something again and again with great force, usually with the fists or a heavy tool
senses.definitionCN: 用拳头或沉重工具反复用力击打某物
senses.example: He pounded the door until someone opened it.
senses.exampleCN: 他不停地擂门，直到有人来开。
senses.why: The beating verb is a separate Old English word, punian, probably imitative of blows; its spelling later merged with the weight word, but the force is its own.
senses.whyCN: 表示击打的动词另有来历，是古英语 punian，一般认为模仿打人的声响；后来拼写与重量词合流，但那股力道是它自带的。

senses.title: To beat with a heavy rhythm
senses.definition: to move or beat with a strong regular force, as a heart or a pair of running feet does
senses.definitionCN: 心脏或奔跑的脚步以强烈而规律的力道跳动、起落
senses.example: Her heart was pounding as she waited for the result.
senses.exampleCN: 等结果的时候，她的心怦怦直跳。
senses.why: Once the verb names repeated heavy blows, the body's own drum can borrow it, because a racing heart is felt as something striking from inside.
senses.whyCN: 动词一旦指反复的重击，身体自己的鼓点就能借用它，因为心跳加速时，人感到的正是有什么在体内一下下撞。

senses.title: To crush something into a paste
senses.definition: to break something into small pieces or a soft mass by hitting it again and again in a mortar
senses.definitionCN: 用杵在臼里反复捶打，把东西碎成小块或软糊
senses.example: Pound the garlic with a little salt before adding the oil.
senses.exampleCN: 加橄榄油之前，先把蒜加一点盐捣碎。
senses.why: Crushing with a pestle is the same downward blow repeated in one small bowl, so the cooking sense keeps the action and changes only the result.
senses.whyCN: 用杵捣东西，就是在小臼里重复同一种向下砸的动作；烹饪义保留了动作，只换了结果。

intro.en: Pound carries two histories that ended up spelled alike: a Latin weight word that became money and mass, and an Old English verb of beating that probably copies the sound of blows.
intro.cn: pound 背着两段最后拼成同一个样子的历史：一个变成货币与重量的拉丁称重词，和一个很可能模仿打击声的古英语动词。

items.en: Pendere meant to hang and also to weigh, since goods were weighed on a hanging balance.
items.cn: pendere 既指悬挂，也指称重，因为货物是挂在秤上称的。

items.en: Pondo, short for libra pondo, meant a pound by weight, and this is the form that gave English the name of the unit.
items.cn: pondo 是 libra pondo 的省略，意为「按重量计的一磅」，英语里这个单位的名字就来自它。

items.en: Libra named both the scales and the Roman pound; its abbreviation lb and the crossed L of the money sign still stand for weight and for sterling.
items.cn: libra 既指天平，也指罗马磅；它的缩写 lb 与货币符号里那个带横杠的 L，至今仍分别代表重量与英镑。

items.en: Old English pund took the Latin weight word and used it for goods on the market and for silver by weight.
items.cn: 古英语 pund 接过这个拉丁重量词，既用于市场上的货物，也用于按重量计的银子。

items.en: A separate verb punian meant to beat or crush, probably imitative; Middle English merged its spelling with pound.
items.cn: 另有一个动词 punian，意为捶打、捣碎，一般认为带拟声性质；中古英语把它的拼写并入了 pound。

items.en: Modern English keeps the amount, the coin, the blows, the heartbeat and the mortar, all under five letters.
items.cn: 现代英语把这几种意思都留在五个字母里：分量、钱币、捶打、心跳与捣臼。

note.en: The look-alike group puts the word's own derivatives beside two spellings that only resemble it; the near-meaning group gathers money words and verbs of beating.
note.cn: 形近组把本词自己的派生词与两个只是拼写相像的词放在一起；近义组收货币词与表示捶打的动词。

entries.definition: Something that weighs or hits a stated number of pounds.
entries.definitionCN: 重达若干磅的东西；捣击者。

entries.definition: Weight measured in pounds, or a charge made by weight.
entries.definitionCN: 以磅计的重量；按重量收取的费用。

entries.definition: To jump on something suddenly and seize it, as a cat does.
entries.definitionCN: 突然扑上去抓住，如猫扑猎物；这只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: To push the lips forward in displeasure.
entries.definitionCN: 不高兴地撅起嘴唇；这只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: British money of standard purity, especially the pound.
entries.definitionCN: 标准纯度的英国货币，尤指英镑。

entries.definition: To hit something heavily, making a dull sound.
entries.definitionCN: 重重地打，发出闷响。

entries.definition: To strike again and again in a regular rhythm.
entries.definitionCN: 以规律节奏反复打击。

entries.definition: To hit something hard with a tool or with force.
entries.definitionCN: 用工具或用力反复敲打。

normalIntro.en: Two strands meet in one spelling: a weighed amount that became money, and a repeated blow that became a heartbeat and a mortar.
normalIntro.cn: 两条线在一个拼写里相遇：一个被称出来的分量变成了钱，一种反复的击打变成了心跳与捣臼。

normal.en: Libra is why the abbreviation lb stands for a pound of weight and why the money sign carries a crossed L.
normal.cn: 正因为 libra，重量单位缩写写作 lb，货币符号里也带着一个带横杠的 L。

normal.en: Pondo meant by weight, so a pound was first a quantity of silver, and only later the coin made from it.
normal.cn: pondo 意为「按重量计」，所以一磅最早是一份银子，后来才指用这份银子铸的钱。

normal.en: The beating pound is a different word, from Old English punian, so no weight is hidden inside pound the door.
normal.cn: 表示捶打的 pound 是另一个词，出自古英语 punian，所以「擂门」那个 pound 里并没有藏着重量的意思。

normal.en: Compare heart pounding and rain pounding on the roof: both describe a heavy rhythm rather than a single blow.
normal.cn: 比较 heart pounding 与雨打屋顶：两者说的都是有节奏的重击，而不是单独一下。

normal.en: Pound the garlic names the same downward stroke a pestle makes in a mortar.
normal.cn: pound the garlic 说的正是杵在臼里那一下下的下砸动作。

abstract.en: A currency named after a weight reminds you that money once had to be put on a scale.
abstract.cn: 一种以重量命名的货币提醒人：钱曾经必须放上秤。

abstract.en: The word holds a scale and a hammer at once, and context decides which one you are holding.
abstract.cn: 这个词同时握着一杆秤和一把锤子，语境决定你手里拿的是哪一样。

abstract.en: A heart pounds in the same rhythm as a fist on a door, which is why one verb serves both.
abstract.cn: 心跳与拳头擂门是同一种节奏，所以一个动词能同时管这两件事。

examples.en: She paid three pounds for the brass scales.
examples.cn: 她花三英镑买下了那杆黄铜秤。

examples.en: He pounded the garlic with a little salt.
examples.cn: 他把蒜加一点盐捣碎。

examples.en: Her heart pounded as the plane touched down.
examples.cn: 飞机落地时，她的心怦怦直跳。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「磅」的读音正好对得上；一磅重的东西砸下来砰的一声，pound 既是磅与英镑，也是猛砸。

root: 重量与货币义来自拉丁语 libra pondo（按重量计的一磅），经古英语 pund 进入英语；猛击义另有来源，一般认为出自古英语 punian（捶打、捣碎），可能为拟声。

sensesIntro.en: The senses split into two groups: a measured amount that turned into money, and a repeated heavy blow that turned into a heartbeat and a pestle.
sensesIntro.cn: 义项分成两群：一个被称出来的分量变成了钱，一种反复的重击变成了心跳与杵。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a brass balance on an old table, its pan pressed low by a heap of coins.
core.cn: 核心意象：旧木桌上一杆黄铜秤，秤盘被一堆硬币压得很低。

branches.en: coins counted twice on a market stall
branches.cn: 摊位上被数了两遍的硬币

branches.en: potatoes dropping one by one onto a scale
branches.cn: 土豆一个个落到秤盘上

branches.en: a fist landing on a locked door
branches.cn: 拳头一下下砸在锁着的门上

branches.en: a pulse felt in the throat while waiting
branches.cn: 等候时喉咙里感到的脉搏

branches.en: a pestle turning garlic into paste
branches.cn: 杵把蒜捣成糊

intro.en: A Latin family of weighing supplies the money and the mass, while the beating verb comes from Old English; English suffixes then build the noise, the tool and the charge.
intro.cn: 一个表示称重的拉丁词族提供了货币与质量义，表示击打的动词则来自古英语；英语后缀再分别造出响声、器具与按磅计的收费。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: a unit of weight or money
weight or charge measured in pounds

definition_zh: 倒；灌；倾泻；大量涌入；倾诉；浇筑
definition_en: to make a liquid flow out of a container, to cause people or things to move in a steady stream, to rain very heavily, to tell feelings freely, or to cast wet concrete
core_image: 一只手把壶嘴压低，水柱落进杯里，杯口腾起一点热气
scene: 屋檐下的水线连成一片，院里的人抱着盆往外泼。It had poured all night, and the lane was ankle-deep in water.
sceneCN: 这里 pour 指「大雨倾盆而下」（第 3 个义项：雨下得又急又密）；句意为雨下了一整夜，巷子里的水已经没到脚踝。图中可辨识场景：连成水线的屋檐、往外泼水的盆、漫过路面的积水。

pos.zh: 倒；灌；倾泻；涌入；倾诉；浇筑

derivatives.zh: 由 down 与 pour 复合而成，义为「倾盆大雨」
由 out 与 pouring 复合而成，义为「倾泻；情感的流露」
由 pour 加表示人或物的 -er 构成，义为「倒液体的人或器具」

senses.title: To make a liquid flow from a container
senses.definition: to hold a container at an angle so that the liquid inside runs out into another vessel
senses.definitionCN: 把容器倾斜，让里面的液体流进另一个器皿
senses.example: She poured the tea slowly so that the leaves stayed in the pot.
senses.exampleCN: 她慢慢地倒茶，让茶叶留在壶里。
senses.why: The oldest recorded use is simply liquid leaving a vessel, and every later sense keeps that picture of something flowing out under control.
senses.whyCN: 有记录的最早用法就是液体离开容器，后来每个义项都保留着这幅画面：有东西在控制之下流出来。

senses.title: To move in a continuous stream
senses.definition: to come or go somewhere in large numbers and without a break, like a liquid that will not stop
senses.definitionCN: 像止不住的液体一样，大批而不间断地来或去
senses.example: Fans poured out of the stadium as the final whistle blew.
senses.exampleCN: 终场哨响，球迷从体育场里涌了出来。
senses.why: A crowd moves like a liquid when it is dense enough, so English uses the same verb for people, letters and money arriving in an unbroken flow.
senses.whyCN: 人群一旦密集，移动起来就像液体，于是英语用同一个动词来说人、信件和钱源源不断地到来。

senses.title: To rain very heavily
senses.definition: to rain hard and steadily, so that water seems to be tipped out of the sky
senses.definitionCN: 雨下得又急又密，仿佛天上有水被整盆倒下
senses.example: It poured all afternoon, and nobody left the house.
senses.exampleCN: 整个下午都在下倾盆大雨，谁也没出门。
senses.why: Rain is water falling in sheets, so the verb of tipping out a vessel transfers to the sky itself, especially in the impersonal phrase it is pouring.
senses.whyCN: 雨就是成片落下的水，于是「把容器倒空」的动词被挪到天上，尤其在 it is pouring 这种无人称说法里。

senses.title: To tell feelings without holding back
senses.definition: to express feelings or a story freely and at length, as if emptying what is inside
senses.definitionCN: 把心里的感受或经历毫无保留地、连续地说出来
senses.example: She poured out the whole story to a friend at the kitchen table.
senses.exampleCN: 她坐在厨房桌边，把整件事都向朋友倾诉了出来。
senses.why: If a vessel can be emptied, so can a person, and pour out turns the chest into a container whose contents finally leave.
senses.whyCN: 容器能被倒空，人也可以；pour out 把胸腔变成一只容器，里面的东西终于流了出来。

senses.title: To cast wet concrete or metal
senses.definition: to fill a mould or a prepared space with wet concrete or molten metal so that it sets into shape
senses.definitionCN: 把湿混凝土或熔化的金属灌进模子或备好的空间，让它凝固成形
senses.example: The crew poured the foundation before the rain came.
senses.exampleCN: 工人在下雨之前浇好了地基。
senses.why: Building work borrows the kitchen verb because wet concrete is a heavy liquid that has to be tipped into a prepared shape and left to harden.
senses.whyCN: 建筑行当借用这个厨房动词，因为湿混凝土就是一种沉重的液体，要倒进备好的形状里，再等它变硬。

intro.en: Pour is a Middle English verb whose origin is uncertain. The usual guess points to Old French, but no link has been proved, and the word has no reliable Latin relative.
intro.cn: pour 是中古英语的一个动词，来源不确定。常见的猜测指向古法语，但没有得到证实，这个词也没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

items.en: Pour first appears around the fourteenth century as pouren, meaning to flow, gush or tip liquid out; the earlier history is not recorded.
items.cn: pour 约在十四世纪以 pouren 的形式出现，意为流出、涌出、把液体倒出；更早的来历没有记录。

items.en: Some dictionaries suggest a link with Old French purer, to pour out or strain, but the connection remains a guess rather than an established borrowing.
items.cn: 有些词典猜测它与古法语 purer（倒出、滤出）有关，但这只是一种猜测，并未确立为借词关系。

items.en: The verb widened from liquid in a cup to crowds leaving a gate and to rain falling in sheets, because all three move in one unbroken flow.
items.cn: 这个动词从杯里的液体扩展到涌出大门的人群与成片落下的雨，因为三者都是不间断地流动。

items.en: With modern building work the verb took on concrete and metal, which are liquids only until they set.
items.cn: 随着近代建筑工程，这个动词用到了混凝土与金属上，而它们只在凝固之前是液体。

items.en: Modern English keeps the physical sense and adds the emotional one, so a person may pour tea, pour out a story, or stand in the pouring rain.
items.cn: 现代英语保留物理义，又添了情感义，所以一个人可以倒茶、倾诉一件事，也可以站在倾盆大雨里。

note.en: The look-alike group puts two spellings that merely sound the same beside the word's own derivatives; the near-meaning group gathers verbs for liquid on the move.
note.cn: 形近组把两个只是读音相同的拼写与本词自己的派生词放在一起；近义组收表示液体流动的动词。

entries.definition: A tiny opening in skin or in a leaf; also to study a text closely.
entries.definitionCN: 皮肤或叶片上的小孔；也指细读；这只是读音相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Having little money or little quality.
entries.definitionCN: 缺钱的；质量差的；这只是读音相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A person or vessel that pours liquid.
entries.definitionCN: 倒液体的人或器具。

entries.definition: A sudden heavy fall of rain.
entries.definitionCN: 突如其来的倾盆大雨。

entries.definition: To let liquid fall out of a container by accident.
entries.definitionCN: 不慎让液体从容器里洒出。

entries.definition: To move steadily and smoothly, as a liquid does.
entries.definitionCN: 像液体一样平稳不断地移动。

entries.definition: To move in a continuous current.
entries.definitionCN: 以连续的水流般移动。

entries.definition: To flow out suddenly and in large amounts.
entries.definitionCN: 突然大量涌出。

normalIntro.en: There is no Latin root to lean on here, so the word is best held by its pictures: a tipped jug, a crowd at a gate, a sky emptied out.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词背后没有拉丁词根可依靠，最好用画面来记住它：倾斜的壶、门口的人群、被倒空的天。

normal.en: Pour out and pour into are the two directions: out of a container, into another place or crowd.
normal.cn: pour out 与 pour into 是两个方向：从容器里出来，进入另一个地方或人群。

normal.en: Downpour adds down to pour, and English rain does fall down, so the compound needs no explanation.
normal.cn: downpour 在 pour 前加 down，英语的雨本来就是往下落的，所以这个复合词不必多解释。

normal.en: Outpouring keeps the same movement for feelings: what was inside comes out in quantity.
normal.cn: outpouring 把同一种流动用在情感上：原本在里面的东西大量地出来了。

normal.en: Pourer adds -er, so the word can name a person or a jug designed to pour cleanly.
normal.cn: pourer 加 -er，于是这个词既能指人，也能指专门设计来倒得干净的壶。

normal.en: It is pouring is impersonal, like it is raining: the sky, not a person, is doing the pouring.
normal.cn: it is pouring 是无人称句，和 it is raining 一样：倒水的是天，不是人。

abstract.en: Pour is what happens when a boundary is opened: a jug, a gate, a heart, a mould.
abstract.cn: pour 说的是边界被打开的那一刻：壶口、门口、心口、模子口。

abstract.en: The same verb covers tea and rain because both are water that has stopped being held.
abstract.cn: 同一个动词能管茶也能管雨，因为两者都是不再被兜住的水。

abstract.en: To pour out a story is to treat words as something liquid and finite, stored until it runs.
abstract.cn: 把故事倾诉出来，就是把话语当成一种有限的水，一直存着，直到流尽。

examples.en: She poured the tea slowly into four cups.
examples.cn: 她把茶慢慢倒进四只杯子里。

examples.en: It poured all night and the lane flooded.
examples.cn: 雨下了一整夜，巷子都淹了。

examples.en: He poured out his worries to an old friend.
examples.cn: 他把心里的烦恼向一位老朋友倾诉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泼」——泼水出去就是 pour；雨大得整盆往下倒，也说 it is pouring。

root: 中古英语 pouren（涌出、倾倒），约十四世纪见于记录，更早来源不确定；有词典猜测与古法语 purer（倒出、滤出）有关，但未成定论，没有可靠的拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The senses all describe something leaving a boundary in a steady flow: liquid, a crowd, rain, feeling, wet concrete.
sensesIntro.cn: 几个义项说的都是某种东西越过边界、连续流出：液体、人群、雨、情感、湿混凝土。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand tipping a jug lower, a thin column of water dropping into a cup.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把壶压得更低，一条细水柱落进杯里。

branches.en: a teapot tilted until the last drop leaves
branches.cn: 茶壶被倾到最后一滴流出

branches.en: a gate opening onto a river of people
branches.cn: 大门打开，人群像河水涌出

branches.en: a gutter overflowing while the sky stays grey
branches.cn: 天还灰着，排水沟已经溢出

branches.en: words coming faster than the listener can nod
branches.cn: 话说得比听的人点头还快

branches.en: wet concrete sliding down a wooden form
branches.cn: 湿混凝土顺着木模滑下

intro.en: With no Latin stem behind it, the word is held together by English pieces: the base verb, its participles, -er for the vessel, and the compounds down and out.
intro.cn: 这个词背后没有拉丁词干，靠英语自身的部件撑起来：基础动词、它的分词、表示器具的 -er，以及 down 与 out 两个复合成分。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: a person or vessel that pours
a flood of feeling or of people

definition_zh: 力量；权力；能力；电力；幂（数学）；（镜头的）放大倍率
definition_en: the ability to act, control or influence, or the energy and mathematical capacity that make action possible
core_image: 一只手握住总闸的把手往下一压，整条街的灯同时亮起
scene: 变电站里，值班员把总闸推上去，整片街区的灯同时亮了。A fallen line cut the power to three streets before dawn.
sceneCN: 这里指「供给电器的电力」（第 4 个义项：电力供应）；句意为天亮前一条掉落的电线切断了三条街的供电。可辨识物件：总闸、变电站、电线、街灯、工具箱；对应第 1 个义项。

forms.label: 不可数用法（力量或电力）
可数复数（多种权力或强国）

derivatives.zh: 强大的；有影响力的
无力的；无权势的
强有力地
由……驱动的
有效的；强有力的（同出「能」词根）
潜力；潜在的

senses.title: Physical force
senses.definition: the strength or energy that something uses to move, break or hold another thing
senses.definitionCN: 某物用于移动、破坏或固定另一物的力量或能量
senses.example: The storm's power tore the roof from the shed.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴的力量把棚屋的屋顶掀掉了。
senses.why: The Latin source means 'to be able'; the first kind of ability is the brute ability to move matter.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁来源意为「能够」；最基础的能力就是移动物体的蛮力。

senses.title: Control over people and decisions
senses.definition: the capacity to make others act or to determine collective decisions, whether through office, money or numbers
senses.definitionCN: 使他人行动或决定集体事务的能力，可来自职位、金钱或人数
senses.example: The union used its power to stop the layoffs.
senses.exampleCN: 工会动用它的力量阻止了裁员。
senses.why: Ability directed at people becomes influence; whoever can change what others do holds power.
senses.whyCN: 指向他人的能力变成影响力；能改变他人行为的人就握有权力。

senses.title: Capacity to produce an effect
senses.definition: the ability of a thing, substance or person to produce a particular effect
senses.definitionCN: 某物、某物质或某人产生特定效果的能力
senses.example: The drug has the power to relieve pain within minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药能在几分钟内缓解疼痛。
senses.why: The same 'can' is at work here: the question is not who commands but what a thing is able to do.
senses.whyCN: 这里仍是同一个「能」：问题不是谁在下命令，而是某物能够做成什么。

senses.title: Electricity supplied to a place
senses.definition: electric energy supplied to homes, machines or a network
senses.definitionCN: 供给住宅、机器或电网的电能
senses.example: A fallen line cut the power to three streets before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 天亮前一条掉落的电线切断了三条街的供电。
senses.why: The industrial age narrowed the general word to the energy that makes machines able to work.
senses.whyCN: 工业时代把这一通用词收窄为让机器得以运转的能量。

senses.title: An exponent in mathematics
senses.definition: the number that shows how many times a base is multiplied by itself
senses.definitionCN: 表示一个底数被自身相乘多少次的数
senses.example: Two raised to the fifth power equals thirty-two.
senses.exampleCN: 二的五次方等于三十二。
senses.why: Repeated multiplication multiplies capacity, so mathematics named the count of multiplications by the same word.
senses.whyCN: 重复相乘使能力成倍增长，因此数学用同一个词来命名相乘的次数。

senses.title: Magnification of a lens
senses.definition: the factor by which an optical instrument enlarges a distant object
senses.definitionCN: 光学仪器把远处物体放大的倍数
senses.example: A ten-power lens brings the distant ridge into view.
senses.exampleCN: 十倍的镜头把远处的山脊拉到眼前。
senses.why: A lens multiplies the reach of the eye, so its factor is also called its power.
senses.whyCN: 镜头把眼睛的触及范围成倍扩大，因此它的倍数也被称为它的力量。

senses.title: A strong state on the world stage
senses.definition: a country able to influence other states through military, economic or diplomatic capacity
senses.definitionCN: 能通过军事、经济或外交能力影响他国的国家
senses.example: The two powers agreed to limit naval forces in the region.
senses.exampleCN: 两个强国同意限制该地区的海军力量。
senses.why: States are treated as single actors, so the ability to act becomes a nation's power.
senses.whyCN: 国家被当作单一行动者，因此行动的能力就成为一个国家的力量。

senses.title: Legal authority to act for another
senses.titleCN: 代他人行动的法定权限
senses.definition: a legal document or status allowing one person to act on another's behalf
senses.definitionCN: 允许一个人代另一人行动的法定文件或身份
senses.example: The daughter held power of attorney for her father.
senses.exampleCN: 女儿持有父亲的授权委托书。
senses.why: Law borrowed the word for a delegated ability: the agent can act because the principal's capacity has been transferred.
senses.whyCN: 法律借用这个词表示被授予的能力：代理人能行动，是因为本人的能力被转交了过来。

intro.en: Power came through Old French poeir from Vulgar Latin potere, from Latin posse 'to be able', built on potis 'able' and esse 'to be'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: power 经古法语 poeir 来自通俗拉丁 potere，再往上出自拉丁 posse「能够」，由 potis「有能力的」与 esse「是」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Potis meant 'able, capable, powerful'. Its pre-Latin origin is reconstructed rather than directly attested.
items.cn: potis 意为「有能力的、能干的、有力量的」。它在拉丁语之前的来源属于重构，而非直接有据。

items.en: Potis plus esse produced posse, the verb 'to be able, can'.
items.cn: potis 加 esse 构成 posse，即动词「能够、可以」。

items.en: Everyday Latin reshaped the verb as potere, which became the ordinary verb for ability in the Romance languages.
items.cn: 通俗拉丁把这个动词改形为 potere，它后来成为罗曼语族中表示能力的常用动词。

items.en: Old French poeir carried both the verb and a noun for ability into English in the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 poeir 在十三世纪把动词以及表示能力的名词一并带入英语。

items.en: Mathematics adopted the word for an exponent in the sixteenth century, and the electrical sense followed with the power grid in the nineteenth.
items.cn: 数学在十六世纪用这个词指幂指数；随着电网出现，电力义在十九世纪跟进。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin and first date): the pre-Latin source of potis is a reconstruction, and no single first citation is fixed for the electrical sense, so dates here are approximations.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源与首见年代）：potis 在拉丁语之前的来源属于重构形式；电力义也没有唯一的最早书证，因此这里给出的年代均为约数。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same 'able' root; group two holds nouns for strength or influence seen from other angles.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「能够」词根的词；第二组是从其他角度表示力量或影响力的名词。

entries.definition: Having great strength or influence; the adjective describes what the noun possesses.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有强大力量或影响力的；形容词描述名词所拥有的东西。

entries.definition: Having no ability to act or change a situation; it is the direct negation of the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 没有能力行动或改变处境的；是这个名词的直接否定。

entries.definition: Means strong in effect, especially of a drug or argument; it shares the Latin root of ability.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「效力强的」，尤指药物或论证；共享表示能力的拉丁词根。

entries.definition: An ability that exists but has not yet been exercised; it is power still folded up.
entries.definitionCN: 已存在但尚未施展的能力；是仍折叠未用的力量。

entries.definition: The physical quality of being strong; it covers muscles and materials rather than decisions.
entries.definitionCN: 身体或结构上的强壮；覆盖肌肉与材料，而非决策。

entries.definition: Physical energy acting on an object, or organized pressure used to compel.
entries.definitionCN: 作用于物体的物理能量，或用来强迫的有组织压力。

entries.definition: Power that is recognized as rightful; power alone can be held without legitimacy.
entries.definitionCN: 被承认正当的权力；单纯的力量可以在缺乏正当性的情况下被持有。

entries.definition: The ability to change opinions or decisions without direct command.
entries.definitionCN: 不靠直接命令而改变意见或决定的能力。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real 'able' root, the real derivatives and the real technical phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的「能够」词根、真实的派生词与真实的技术搭配。

normal.en: The Latin verb means 'to be able'; every sense is a kind of ability, from moving a roof to lighting a street.
normal.cn: 拉丁动词意为「能够」；每个义项都是一种能力，从掀翻屋顶到点亮街道。

normal.en: The family runs power, powerful, powerless, powerfully, powered, potent and potential.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 power、powerful、powerless、powerfully、powered、potent 与 potential。

normal.en: The political phrases are political power, balance of power and the powers.
normal.cn: 政治搭配有政治权力、力量均势与列强。

normal.en: The technical phrases are power supply, nuclear power and to the power of.
normal.cn: 技术搭配有电源、核能与……次方。

normal.en: The legal phrase is power of attorney, where one person acts for another.
normal.cn: 法律搭配是授权委托书，即一个人代另一个人行动。

abstract.en: Picture a hand on a master switch that lights a whole street at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手按在总闸上，一下点亮整条街。

abstract.en: Picture a number multiplied by itself again and again until it fills the page.
abstract.cn: 想象一个数反复自乘，直到写满整页。

abstract.en: Picture a signature that lets one person stand in another's shoes at a counter.
abstract.cn: 想象一个签名，让一个人在柜台前站进另一个人的位置。

examples.en: The engine's power is measured in kilowatts rather than horses.
examples.cn: 这台发动机的功率用千瓦而非马力来衡量。

examples.en: The committee has no power to change the budget on its own.
examples.cn: 委员会无权自行改变预算。

examples.en: Three to the fourth power is eighty-one.
examples.cn: 三的四次方是八十一。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「能够」加「力」——能推动物体、能让人服从、能让灯亮 → 力量、权力、电力

root: power 经古法语来自通俗拉丁 potere，源头是拉丁 posse「能够」= potis「有能力的」+ esse「是」。potis 在拉丁语之前的来源属于重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one root idea, 'being able': able to move matter, able to command people, able to produce an effect, able to supply electricity, able to multiply a number, able to enlarge an image, able to act as a state, able to act for another person.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个词根观念「能够」展开：能移动物体、能命令他人、能产生效果、能供电、能使数字成倍、能放大图像、能作为国家行动、能代他人行动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand on a master switch.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手按在总闸上。

branches.en: THE BODY'S ABILITY: force that moves or breaks matter is the first meaning of being able.
branches.cn: 身体的能力：移动或破坏物体的力量，是「能够」的第一层含义。

branches.en: THE SOCIAL ABILITY: a union or a state acts because people and institutions can be made to move.
branches.cn: 社会的能力：工会或国家能行动，是因为可以使人及机构动起来。

branches.en: THE EFFECT: a drug or a word is powerful when it can change a body or a mind.
branches.cn: 效果：药物或言辞之所以有力，是因为它能改变身体或心智。

branches.en: THE CURRENT: the industrial age gave the general word to the energy that runs machines.
branches.cn: 电流：工业时代把这一通用词交给了驱动机器的能量。

branches.en: THE MEASURED AND DELEGATED: an exponent multiplies a number, a lens multiplies sight, and a legal document transfers capacity.
branches.cn: 可计量与可转交：指数使数字成倍，镜头使视力成倍，法律文件则转交能力。

intro.en: The word can be read from a Latin adjective of ability, the verb 'to be', the compound verb they form and the modern derived family.
intro.cn: 这个单词可以按表示能力的拉丁形容词、表示「是」的动词、由它们合成的动词以及现代派生词族逐段读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin potis and esse give posse, the source of power; the same stem yields potent, potential and the noun potentia.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 potis 与 esse 构成 posse，也就是 power 的来源；同一词干还衍生 potent、potential 与名词 potentia。

items.example: The adjective supplied the idea of capability.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词提供「有能力」的观念。

items.example: The verb completes the compound meaning 'to be able'.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词补足「能够」的合成含义。

items.example: The Latin verb stated plain ability.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词表示单纯的能力。

items.example: The noun named capacity as a quality.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指作为一种性质的能力。

items.example: The motor lost power on the climb.
items.exampleCN: 马达在爬坡时失去了动力。

items.example: A powerful storm crossed the coast.
The villagers felt powerless against the landslide.
items.exampleCN: 村民面对山体滑坡感到无能为力。

items.example: The speech argued powerfully for the bridge.
items.exampleCN: 这场演讲为这座桥做了有力的论证。

items.example: The shed runs on solar-powered lights.
items.exampleCN: 棚屋使用太阳能驱动的灯。

items.example: The drug is potent at a very low dose.
items.exampleCN: 这种药在很低的剂量下就有效。

definition_zh: 练习；实践；惯例；诊所；执业
definition_en: the repeated doing of an activity to improve a skill, the actual carrying out of an idea, a usual way of doing things, or the professional work and workplace of a doctor or lawyer
core_image: 同一段音阶被反复弹到手指自己记住，琴键上留下浅浅的指痕
scene: 琴房窗外已经黑透，节拍器还在一下一下地摆，女孩把同一段音阶又弹了一遍。Her daily practice on the piano lasts forty minutes, even on holidays.
sceneCN: 这里 practice 是「练习」（第 1 个义项：为熟练而反复做某事）；句意为她每天在钢琴上练习四十分钟，节假日也不间断。画面里有黑透的窗、摆动的节拍器和反复弹奏的音阶。

pos.zh: 练习；实践；惯例；诊所；执业

derivatives.zh: 由 practice 的词干 practic- 加形容词后缀 -al 构成，义为「实际的；实用的」
practical 加 -ly 构成，义为「几乎；实际上」
由 practice 的词干加表示从业者的后缀构成，义为「从业者；执业医生」
英式拼写中以 -ise 结尾的动词形式，义为「练习；执业」，美式统一写 practice

senses.title: Repeated exercise to improve a skill
senses.definition: the repeated doing of an activity in order to become better at it
senses.definitionCN: 为了变得更熟练而反复进行某项活动
senses.example: Daily practice is the only way to play that passage smoothly.
senses.exampleCN: 每日练习是把这个乐段弹流畅的唯一办法。
senses.why: The Greek root meant doing rather than knowing, so practice begins as action repeated until the body remembers it.
senses.whyCN: 希腊词根强调的是一遍遍去做，而不是想明白，所以 practice 的起点是反复行动，直到身体自己记住。

senses.title: The actual doing of an idea
senses.definition: the carrying out of a plan, belief or method in real situations rather than only talking about it
senses.definitionCN: 把计划、信念或方法放到真实情境中实行，而不只是谈论
senses.example: The new rules look fair on paper but are hard in practice.
senses.exampleCN: 新规定在纸面上看着公平，实践起来却很难。
senses.why: If the core is repeated action, the same noun can name the moment an idea leaves the page and turns into something done.
senses.whyCN: 既然核心是反复的行动，这个名词也就能指想法离开纸面、变成实际行动的那一刻。

senses.title: A usual way of doing things
senses.definition: a habit or accepted custom, especially one followed by a group or a profession
senses.definitionCN: 习惯或被普遍接受的做法，尤指某一群体或行业沿用的方式
senses.example: It is common practice to confirm a booking by email.
senses.exampleCN: 用电子邮件确认预订是常见的做法。
senses.why: What is done again and again hardens into a rule, so practice slides from one person's repetition to a group's settled custom.
senses.whyCN: 反复去做的事会慢慢固化成规矩，于是 practice 从一个人的重复，滑向一群人的既定惯例。

senses.title: The business of a professional
senses.definition: the work of a doctor or lawyer, and the place where that work is done
senses.definitionCN: 医生或律师所从事的工作，以及开展这项工作的场所
senses.example: She runs a small practice in the town centre.
senses.exampleCN: 她在市中心经营一家小诊所。
senses.why: A profession rests on practised skill, so the word comes to name the professional's ongoing work and the rooms where it happens.
senses.whyCN: 一门职业建立在反复练就的本领之上，所以这个词又用来指专业人士长期从事的业务，以及开展业务的场所。

intro.en: Practice travels through Latin and French back to a Greek word for doing, and its modern spelling split belongs to English alone.
intro.cn: practice 经拉丁语和法语上溯到希腊语中表示「做」的词，而它现代拼写的分工是英语自己后来形成的。

items.en: The verb prassein, in its Attic form prattein, meant to do, to act or to achieve, and it is the earliest recoverable source of the family.
items.cn: 动词 prassein（阿提卡方言作 prattein）意为做、行动、完成，是这一族词最早可追溯的来源。

items.en: The adjective praktikos described a person or thing fit for action, as opposed to merely theoretical.
items.cn: 形容词 praktikos 形容适合行动的、能实干的，与只停留在理论上的东西相对。

items.en: Latin took praktikos as practicus, and medieval Latin formed the noun practica for practical knowledge or the actual doing of something.
items.cn: 拉丁语把 praktikos 借作 practicus，中世纪拉丁语又造出名词 practica，指实用知识或实际去做。

items.en: Old French practique and the verb practiser carried the words into daily use, and English borrowed both in the centuries after the Norman settlement.
items.cn: 古法语 practique 与动词 practiser 把这些词带入日常使用，英语在诺曼人定居后的几个世纪里把两者都借了进来。

items.en: British English keeps practice for the noun and practise for the verb, while American English uses practice for both; the -ice and -ise endings are the everyday marker of that division.
items.cn: 英式英语用 practice 作名词、practise 作动词，美式英语则名词动词都写 practice；-ice 与 -ise 两种词尾就是这一分工的日常标记。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the spelling pair and the Latin-derived family; the near-meaning group gathers words for training, habit and real application.
note.cn: 形近组收这一对拼写以及拉丁来源的词族；近义组收表示训练、习惯与真正实行的词。

entries.definition: The British verb form, used for doing an activity repeatedly or working in a profession.
entries.definitionCN: 英式动词拼写，表示反复做某事或在某一行业执业。

entries.definition: Concerned with real action rather than with theory.
entries.definitionCN: 关乎实际行动而非理论的；实用的。

entries.definition: A person who works in a profession such as medicine or law.
entries.definitionCN: 从事医学、法律等职业的人；从业者。

entries.definition: A course of supervised practical work for students.
entries.definitionCN: 学生在督导下进行的实习课程。

entries.definition: Activity done repeatedly to train the body or the mind.
entries.definitionCN: 为训练身体或头脑而反复进行的活动。

entries.definition: A run-through of a performance before the real one.
entries.definitionCN: 正式演出之前的排练。

entries.definition: Something a person does regularly, often without thinking about it.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人经常做、往往不假思索的事。

entries.definition: An accepted way of behaving in a group or a society.
entries.definitionCN: 群体或社会中已被接受的行为方式。

normalIntro.en: The word is held together by a Greek verb for doing, a Latin adjective for fitness to act, and an English split between the noun and the verb.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由表示「做」的希腊动词、表示「适于行动」的拉丁形容词，以及英语里名词与动词的拼写分工共同支撑。

normal.en: Greek prattein means to do, so practice is tied to action from the start rather than to theory.
normal.cn: 希腊语 prattein 意为做，所以 practice 从一开始就绑在行动上，而不是理论上。

normal.en: Latin practicus meant fit for action, and English practical keeps that sense of something usable rather than abstract.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 practicus 意为适于行动的，英语 practical 保留了「能用得上」而不是「抽象」的意味。

normal.en: British English marks the job with -ise: practise is the verb and practice is the noun.
normal.cn: 英式英语用 -ise 标出动词身份：practise 是动词，practice 是名词。

normal.en: American English drops the distinction and writes practice for both, which is why a spell-checker may object to practise.
normal.cn: 美式英语不分名词动词，一律写 practice，所以拼写检查常常会对 practise 提出异议。

normal.en: Practitioner adds a person suffix to the same stem and names someone who practises a profession.
normal.cn: practitioner 在同一词干后加上表示人的后缀，指从事某一职业的人。

abstract.en: Picture a pianist's fingers finding the keys without the eyes: practice is memory stored in the body.
abstract.cn: 想象钢琴家的手指不看琴键也能落准：practice 就是存进身体里的记忆。

abstract.en: A plan on paper becomes practice the moment someone follows it out in the rain.
abstract.cn: 纸上的计划，在有人冒着雨照着去做的那一刻才成为 practice。

abstract.en: A clinic is called a practice because a doctor's skill stays alive through seeing patients, not through holding a certificate.
abstract.cn: 诊所之所以叫 practice，是因为医生的本领靠一次次接诊维持，而不是靠一张证书。

examples.en: Her daily practice on the piano lasts forty minutes.
examples.cn: 她每天在钢琴上练习四十分钟。

examples.en: The rule works well in practice.
examples.cn: 这条规则在实践中效果很好。

examples.en: He joined a small legal practice after graduating.
examples.cn: 毕业后他加入了一家小型律师事务所。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑来个题」——考前扑来一堆题，正好拿来练手；记住 practice 是练习。

root: 希腊语 prassein/prattein（做、行动）→ 形容词 praktikos（适于行动的）→ 拉丁语 practicus 与中世纪拉丁语名词 practica（实用知识、实行）→ 古法语 practique/practiser → 英语 practice/practise。英式分工为名词 practice、动词 practise，美式为两者皆写 practice。

sensesIntro.en: The core is repeated action; from it come the doing of an idea, the custom that repetition creates, and the professional work built on practised skill.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是反复的行动；由此长出把想法付诸实行、重复所养成的惯例，以及建立在熟练本领之上的专业执业。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the same scale played again and again until the fingers remember it.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一段音阶被反复弹奏，直到手指自己记住。

branches.en: a metronome ticking beside a closed piano lid
branches.cn: 合上的琴盖旁，节拍器还在响

branches.en: a printed rule stepped on by wet boots
branches.cn: 印着规则的纸被湿靴子踩过

branches.cn: 每家店门口重复的同一句招呼

branches.cn: 摆着三把椅子和一块名牌的候诊室

intro.en: A Greek verb of doing, a Latin adjective of practical fitness and two rival English endings carry the whole word.
intro.cn: 一个表示「做」的希腊动词、一个表示「适于实干」的拉丁形容词，加上两种相互竞争的英语词尾，撑起了整个词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin and medieval Latin layers are well recorded and supply both the adjective and the noun behind this word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语与中世纪拉丁语这两层有清楚记录，为这个词提供了形容词与名词两个来源。

items.meaning: to do repeatedly, to work in a profession

items.meaningCN: 名词词尾：状态、性质、事物

definition_zh: 练习；执业；奉行；施展（手法）
definition_en: the British spelling of the verb meaning to do something repeatedly in order to improve, to work as a doctor or lawyer, to follow a religion or custom, or to perform a trick
core_image: 一个人对着镜子把同一句台词念到嘴唇自己会动，镜面上全是呼出的白雾
scene: 剧场后台只剩一盏化妆灯，演员对着镜子把同一句台词又念了一遍，声音沙哑却没有停。She practises the line until it sounds like a thought rather than a recitation.
sceneCN: 这里 practise 是「练习」（第 1 个义项：为熟练而反复做某事）；句意为她反复练那句台词，直到它听起来像临时想到的，而不是背出来的。画面里有化妆灯、镜子和沙哑的嗓音。

pos.zh: 练习；执业；奉行；施展（手法）

derivatives.zh: 由 practise 的过去分词转作形容词，义为「熟练的；老练的」
由 practise 的现在分词转作形容词，义为「执业中的；正在从事某职业的」
英式英语中与动词 practise 分工的名词形式，义为「练习；实践；诊所」
由 practise 的词干加表示从业者的后缀构成，义为「从业者」

senses.title: To do something repeatedly in order to improve
senses.definition: to do an activity many times so that your skill at it improves
senses.definitionCN: 反复进行某项活动，使自己的技能有所提高
senses.example: She practises the violin for an hour before breakfast.
senses.exampleCN: 她早饭前练一个小时小提琴。
senses.why: The Greek source meant to do, so the verb starts from the plain act of doing a thing over and over rather than from thinking about it.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语来源意为「做」，所以这个动词的起点就是把一件事一遍遍做下去，而不是在脑子里琢磨。

senses.title: To work in a profession
senses.definition: to work as a doctor, lawyer or other trained professional
senses.definitionCN: 以医生、律师或其他受过训练的专业人士身份工作
senses.example: He has practised law in this city for twenty years.
senses.exampleCN: 他在这个城市当了二十年律师。
senses.why: Professional work is skill applied daily, so the verb that means repeating an action also names the lifelong carrying out of a trained job.
senses.whyCN: 专业工作就是每天把本领用出来，所以表示反复练习的动词，也用来指把受训得来的职业做一辈子。

senses.title: To follow a religion or custom
senses.definition: to observe the rules and ceremonies of a religion or a traditional custom
senses.definitionCN: 遵守某种宗教或传统习俗的规矩与仪式
senses.example: Her family still practises the old harvest festival.
senses.exampleCN: 她家仍然遵行古老的丰收节习俗。
senses.why: A custom survives only by being done again each year, and the verb for repeated doing fits that annual repetition exactly.
senses.whyCN: 习俗只有年年重新做一遍才能延续，而表示反复去做的动词，正好贴合这种一年一度的重复。

senses.title: To carry out a trick or method
senses.definition: to perform a trick or use a method, especially one that is repeated on new victims
senses.definitionCN: 施展某种手法或使用某种办法，尤指把同一套把戏用在新的对象身上
senses.example: The swindler practised the same trick on three families.
senses.exampleCN: 那个骗子把同一套把戏用在了三户人家身上。
senses.why: If the core is doing something again and again, the word can also describe a trick worked repeatedly on whoever comes next.
senses.whyCN: 既然核心是一遍遍去做，这个词也就能描述一套把戏，反复用在下一个上钩的人身上。

intro.en: Practise shares its whole history with practice, but English sends the verb down the -ise path and keeps -ice for the noun.
intro.cn: practise 与 practice 共享全部历史，只是英语让动词走 -ise 一路，把 -ice 留给名词。

items.en: The verb prassein, Attic prattein, meant to do or to achieve, and the whole family grows from the idea of action.
items.cn: 动词 prassein（阿提卡方言 prattein）意为做、完成，整个词族都从这个「行动」的念头长出来。

items.en: Praktikos described what is fit for action, a word about real work rather than abstract knowledge.
items.cn: praktikos 形容适合行动的，说的是实际动手，而不是抽象知识。

items.en: Latin practicus and the medieval verb practicare named practical action, and the noun practica named the knowledge gained by doing.
items.cn: 拉丁语 practicus 与中世纪动词 practicare 指实际去做，名词 practica 则指通过实践得来的知识。

items.en: Old French practiser, also written pratiquer, meant to put into practice or to carry on a profession, and English took the verb form from it.
items.cn: 古法语 practiser（也写作 pratiquer）意为付诸实践或从事某职业，英语的动词形式就是从它借来的。

items.en: Middle English practisen settled into practise, and British English now keeps practise for the verb while American English uses practice for both; the split is a spelling convention, not a difference in meaning.
items.cn: 中古英语 practisen 定型为 practise，如今英式英语用 practise 作动词、practice 作名词，美式英语两者都写 practice；这一分工只是拼写惯例，并不带来含义差别。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the noun twin and the Latin-derived family; the near-meaning group gathers verbs for training, drilling and carrying something out.
note.cn: 形近组收与它配对的名词形式以及拉丁来源的词族；近义组收表示训练、操练与执行的动词。

entries.definition: The noun in British English, and both noun and verb in American English.
entries.definitionCN: 英式英语中的名词，在美式英语中则名词动词同形。

entries.definition: Useful and concerned with real action rather than theory.
entries.definitionCN: 有用的、关乎实际行动而非理论的。

entries.definition: A person who practises a profession such as medicine or law.
entries.definitionCN: 从事医学、法律等职业的从业者。

entries.definition: A period of supervised practical training for students.
entries.definitionCN: 学生接受督导的实践训练期。

entries.definition: To practise a performance before showing it to an audience.
entries.definitionCN: 在观众面前演出之前进行排练。

entries.definition: To teach and exercise someone over time for a skill or a job.
entries.definitionCN: 用一段时间教导并训练某人掌握技能或胜任工作。

entries.definition: To make someone repeat an exercise until it becomes automatic.
entries.definitionCN: 让人反复做同一练习直到变成自动反应。

entries.definition: To perform a plan, order or method in real life.
entries.definitionCN: 在现实中执行计划、命令或方法。

normalIntro.en: The verb keeps the Greek sense of doing, the Latin layer of practical action, and a British spelling rule that separates it from the noun.
normalIntro.cn: 这个动词保留了希腊语「做」的意思与拉丁语「实际行动」这一层，再加一条把它跟名词分开的英式拼写规则。

normal.en: Practise uses -ise because British English marks verbs with that ending, as in realise and organise.
normal.cn: practise 用 -ise，是因为英式英语用这个词尾标记动词，就像 realise 与 organise。

normal.en: Practice uses -ice because it is the noun, just as advice is the noun beside the verb advise.
normal.cn: practice 用 -ice，因为它是名词，就像 advice 是名词、advise 是动词一样。

normal.en: American English uses practice for the verb too, so only British texts insist on the s.
normal.cn: 美式英语的动词也写 practice，所以只有英式文本才坚持用 s。

normal.en: The -ed form practised keeps the s and doubles nothing: practise, practised, practising.
normal.cn: 加 -ed 的过去式 practised 保留 s，也不双写任何字母：practise、practised、practising。

normal.en: Practise what you preach is the idiom that shows the plainest sense: do the thing, do not just talk about it.
normal.cn: practise what you preach 这个说法体现了最朴素的一层：真去做，而不只是嘴上讲。

abstract.en: A mirror in a cold dressing room is where skill is built: the same line, the same breath, again.
abstract.cn: 冷清的化妆间里那面镜子，就是本领被磨出来的地方：同一句词、同一口气，再来一遍。

abstract.en: A licence on the wall means nothing until the lawyer practises daily in front of real clients.
abstract.cn: 墙上的执照本身不算什么，直到律师每天在真实的当事人面前执业。

abstract.en: A custom lives only while someone practises it, which is why the verb also means to keep a tradition going.
abstract.cn: 习俗只有在有人继续照做时才活着，所以这个动词也意味着把传统延续下去。

examples.en: She practises the violin for an hour before breakfast.
examples.cn: 她早饭前练一个小时小提琴。

examples.en: He has practised law in this city for twenty years.
examples.cn: 他在这个城市当了二十年律师。

examples.en: The swindler practised the same trick on three families.
examples.cn: 那个骗子把同一套把戏用在了三户人家身上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑来个试」——一个接一个的试验扑过来，练的就是手上功夫；记住 practise 是练习。

root: 与 practice 同源：希腊语 prassein/prattein（做）→ praktikos（适于行动的）→ 拉丁语 practicus → 中世纪拉丁语 practica/practicare → 古法语 practiser → 中古英语 practisen。英式英语中动词固定写作 practise、名词写作 practice；美式英语动词与名词都写 practice。

sensesIntro.en: The core is doing a thing over and over; the senses run from training a skill, to living by a profession, to keeping a custom, to working a trick on new victims.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是把一件事反复做下去；义项从磨练技能，延伸到以某职业为生、遵行某种习俗，再到把一套把戏用在新的对象身上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a performer repeating one line at a mirror until the words come without effort.
core.cn: 核心意象：演员对着镜子重复同一句台词，直到字句毫不费力地出来。

branches.en: a mirror, a lamp and one line said thirty times
branches.cn: 一面镜子、一盏灯和一句念了三十遍的台词

branches.en: a brass plate on a solicitor's door
branches.cn: 律师门上一块黄铜名牌

branches.en: a family bowing at the same hour each week
branches.cn: 一家人每周同一时刻躬身

branches.en: the same trick played on a third stranger
branches.cn: 同一个把戏用在第三个陌生人身上

branches.en: hours of drill turning into a licence to work
branches.cn: 长时间操练换来一张执业许可

intro.en: A Greek verb of doing, a Latin verb of practical action, and the English verb ending -ise hold this spelling together.
intro.cn: 一个表示「做」的希腊动词、一个表示实际施行的拉丁动词，以及英语的动词词尾 -ise，共同撑起了这个拼写。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies the adjective practicus and the medieval verb practicare, both built on the idea of practical action.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了形容词 practicus 与中世纪动词 practicare，两者都建立在「实际去做」这一念头上。

items.meaning: to do repeatedly, to work in a profession

definition_zh: 赞美；表扬；赞颂；称赞的话
definition_en: to express strong approval or admiration for someone or something, or the words and worship that express it
core_image: 一群人把手举向台上，掌声像把某个人轻轻托高了一点
scene: 演出结束后全场站起来，掌声持续了很久，主唱却先转身向身后的年轻鼓手鞠了一躬。The crowd praised the drummer more than the singer they had come to see.
sceneCN: 这里 praise 是「称赞、表扬」（第 1 个义项：用言语表达赞许）；句意为观众对那位鼓手的称赞甚至超过他们专程来看的主唱。画面里有起立的观众、持续的掌声和转身鞠躬的主唱。

derivatives.zh: praise 与 worthy 复合而成，义为「值得称赞的」
praise 加表示人的 -er 构成，义为「赞美者」
praise 加 -ful 构成，义为「充满赞美的」（较少使用）

senses.title: To express approval or admiration
senses.definition: to say that someone or something is good, or that you admire them
senses.definitionCN: 说某人或某物很好，或表达对他们的钦佩
senses.example: The teacher praised her for finishing the difficult task alone.
senses.exampleCN: 老师表扬她独自完成了那项困难的任务。
senses.why: The word began as a way of setting a value on something, so praise is literally saying how much someone is worth.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是给某物定价的说法，所以 praise 字面上就是在说某个人值多少。

senses.title: Words that express approval
senses.definition: spoken or written words that show approval or admiration
senses.definitionCN: 口头上或书面上表达赞许与钦佩的话语
senses.example: Her first novel received high praise from several critics.
senses.exampleCN: 她的第一部小说得到了几位评论家的高度赞扬。
senses.why: Once the verb names the act of valuing, the same word can name the words that carry that valuation into public.
senses.whyCN: 动词既指「给出评价」这个动作，同一个词也就能指把这份评价带到人前的话语。

senses.title: To honour God in worship
senses.definition: to give honour and thanks to God, especially in a religious service
senses.definitionCN: 向上帝献上尊崇与感恩，尤指在宗教仪式中
senses.example: The congregation stood to praise God with a slow hymn.
senses.exampleCN: 会众起立，用一首缓慢的赞美诗颂扬上帝。
senses.why: Valuing something highly leads naturally to worship, so the word is used for the honour offered to a deity.
senses.whyCN: 把某样东西看得极高，自然会走向敬拜，于是这个词也用于向神灵献上的尊崇。

senses.title: Worship offered as an act
senses.definition: the honour and worship given to God, or a song or speech used for that purpose
senses.definitionCN: 献给上帝的尊崇与敬拜，或用于这一目的的诗歌与言辞
senses.example: The old book opens with a hymn of praise.
senses.exampleCN: 这本旧书以一首赞颂诗开篇。
senses.why: The noun keeps the religious branch alive beside the everyday one, especially in fixed phrases about worship.
senses.whyCN: 名词把宗教这一支与日常用法并存保留下来，尤其在关于敬拜的固定说法里。

intro.en: Praise comes from Latin words for price and value, passes through French, and still carries the idea of setting a worth on someone.
intro.cn: praise 来自拉丁语中表示价格与价值的词，经法语传入英语，至今仍带着「给某人估定价值」的意思。

items.en: Latin pretium meant price, value or worth, and it stands behind a whole family of words about judging what something is worth.
items.cn: 拉丁语 pretium 意为价格、价值、分量，一整族表示「判断某物值多少」的词都从它而来。

items.en: Late Latin formed the verb pretiare, to value or to set a price on, which carried the idea into action.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语构成动词 pretiare，意为估价、给某物定价，把这个念头带进了动作。

items.en: Old French preisier meant to prize, to value and also to commend, and the sense of speaking well of someone grew out of the sense of valuing.
items.cn: 古法语 preisier 意为珍视、看重，也指称许；「说某人好话」这一层就是从「看重」长出来的。

items.en: Middle English preisen kept both the older sense of valuing and the newer sense of commending, and the spelling settled as praise.
items.cn: 中古英语 preisen 同时保留较早的「看重」与较新的「称许」，拼写后来定型为 praise。

items.en: Modern English keeps praise for spoken approval and for worship, while the old price sense survives in price, prize and appraise.
items.cn: 现代英语用 praise 表示口头赞许与敬拜，而古老的「价格」义则存活在 price、prize 与 appraise 里。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the Latin family of valuing; the near-meaning group gathers verbs and nouns of approval and worship.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁语中表示「估价」的词族；近义组收表示赞许与敬拜的动词和名词。

entries.definition: To judge the value or quality of something.
entries.definitionCN: 评估某物的价值或质量。

entries.definition: To recognize the value of something and be grateful for it.
entries.definitionCN: 认识到某物的价值并心怀感激。

entries.definition: The amount of money that something costs.
entries.definitionCN: 某物花费的金额；价格。

entries.definition: Something valuable given as a reward, or something held dear.
entries.definitionCN: 作为奖励的贵重之物，或被人珍视的东西。

entries.definition: To praise someone formally or officially.
entries.definitionCN: 正式或官方地称赞某人。

entries.definition: To clap in approval, or to praise a decision publicly.
entries.definitionCN: 鼓掌表示赞许，或公开称赞某项决定。

entries.definition: A polite remark that expresses admiration.
entries.definitionCN: 表达钦佩的礼貌话语。

entries.definition: The honour and love given to a god or to someone greatly admired.
entries.definitionCN: 献给神灵或极受崇敬之人的尊崇与热爱。

normalIntro.en: The word joins a Latin noun for price, a late verb for valuing and a French verb for prizing, with an English suffix for worth built on top.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词把表示价格的拉丁名词、表示估价的晚期拉丁动词、表示珍视的法语动词合在一起，又在上面加了表示「值得」的英语后缀。

normal.en: Latin pretium is price, so to praise someone is to say that their worth is high.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 pretium 是价格，所以 praise 一个人就是说他的价值很高。

normal.en: The same root gives price, prize and appraise, all of them about judging value.
normal.cn: 同一词根还给出 price、prize 与 appraise，全都与判断价值有关。

normal.en: Old French preisier meant both to value and to commend, and English kept both senses.
normal.cn: 古法语 preisier 既指看重也指称许，英语把两层都保留了下来。

normal.en: Praiseworthy joins praise and worthy, so it literally means worth praising.
normal.cn: praiseworthy 由 praise 与 worthy 拼合，字面就是「值得称赞的」。

normal.en: Praise is usually uncountable, but praises appears in phrases such as sing someone's praises.
normal.cn: praise 通常不可数，但 praises 会出现在 sing someone's praises 这类说法里。

abstract.en: Applause is value made audible: two hands striking together put a price on a performance.
abstract.cn: 掌声是价值发出了声音：两只手一拍，就等于给一场表演标了价。

abstract.en: Praise costs the speaker almost nothing and can still change what a person believes about themselves.
abstract.cn: 赞美几乎不花说话人什么成本，却仍能改变一个人对自己的看法。

abstract.en: A hymn of praise and a review of a novel use one word because both lift something above the ordinary.
abstract.cn: 赞美诗与小说评论用的是同一个词，因为两者都把某样东西托到平常之上。

examples.en: The crowd praised the drummer more than the singer.
examples.cn: 观众对鼓手的称赞甚至超过了主唱。

examples.en: Her first novel received high praise from several critics.
examples.cn: 她的第一部小说得到了几位评论家的高度赞扬。

examples.en: The congregation stood to praise God with a slow hymn.
examples.cn: 会众起立，用一首缓慢的赞美诗颂扬上帝。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑来事」——好事扑到眼前，当然要夸一夸；记住 praise 是赞美。

root: 拉丁语 pretium（价格、价值）→ 晚期拉丁语 pretiare（估价、看重）→ 古法语 preisier（珍视、称许）→ 中古英语 preisen（看重、赞美）→ 现代英语 praise。同族的 price、prize、appraise、appreciate 都还带着「估定价值」的影子。

sensesIntro.en: The core is setting a high value on someone; it branches into spoken approval, the words themselves, and the honour given in worship.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是给某人估定很高的价值；由此分出当面的赞许、承载赞许的话语，以及献给神灵的崇敬。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a room of people lifting their hands in applause toward one person.
core.cn: 核心意象：满场的人抬手鼓掌，把掌声举向台上的一个人。

branches.en: a teacher nodding at a finished page

definition_zh: 预测；预言；预报；预料；预示
definition_en: to say or state in advance that something will happen, especially on the basis of evidence or reasoning
core_image: 站在今天，用话把明天的那件事先说出来
scene: 经济学家预测明年的增长会放缓。Economists predict slower growth next year.
sceneCN: 这里 predict 是「依据数据对将来作出判断」（第 2 个义项：预测）；句意：经济学家预测明年增长会放缓。场景要点：用现有信息、指向未来、可被检验；对应第 1 个义项。

derivatives.zh: 预测；预言
可预测的；意料之中的
预测者；预测指标
不可预测的；变化莫测的

senses.title: To say what will happen
senses.titleCN: 预测：先说将来会发生什么
senses.definition: to state in advance that a particular event will happen
senses.definitionCN: 事先说明某个特定事件将会发生
senses.example: No one could predict which team would win.
senses.exampleCN: 没有人能预测哪支队伍会赢。
senses.why: Latin praedicere is prae 'before' plus dicere 'say'. The plain sense is saying something before it becomes true.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 praedicere 是 prae“在前”加 dicere“说”。最朴素的意思，就是在事情成真之前先把它说出来。

senses.title: To forecast from evidence
senses.titleCN: 预测：拿现有信息推算未来
senses.definition: to estimate a future state on the basis of data, models, or reasoning
senses.definitionCN: 依据数据、模型或推理估计未来的状况
senses.example: Economists predict slower growth next year.
senses.exampleCN: 经济学家预测明年增长会放缓。
senses.why: The saying is not a guess but a calculation. Evidence is fed in, and the statement about the future comes out.
senses.whyCN: 这话不是猜的，而是算的。把证据喂进去，关于未来的陈述就出来了。

senses.title: Scientific prediction
senses.titleCN: 科学预言：理论先说出可检验的结果
senses.definition: to derive a testable consequence from a scientific theory before it is observed
senses.definitionCN: 在观察之前，从科学理论推出一个可检验的结果
senses.example: The theory predicted a new particle, which was found years later.
senses.exampleCN: 该理论预言了一种新粒子，数年后被找到。
senses.why: A good theory must be able to say what will be seen. Prediction is the test that separates science from speculation.
senses.whyCN: 好的理论必须能说出将会看到什么。预测是把科学与空想分开的那场考试。

senses.title: To indicate in advance by signs
senses.titleCN: 预示：迹象先替将来开口
senses.definition: to be a sign that something will happen, without anyone saying it in words
senses.definitionCN: 成为某事将会发生的迹象，而非由人用话说出
senses.example: Dark clouds predicted a heavy storm.
senses.exampleCN: 乌云预示着大风暴。
senses.why: Signs can speak. When the world itself shows what is coming, we extend the verb from the speaker to the evidence.
senses.whyCN: 迹象也能说话。当世界本身显露出即将发生的事，我们就把这个动词从说话者扩展到证据上。

senses.title: To prophesy
senses.titleCN: 预言：以先知的口吻宣告
senses.definition: to foretell future events as a prophet or oracle does, often without evidence
senses.definitionCN: 像先知或神谕那样预告未来，常无证据支持
senses.example: The old woman predicted that the drought would last seven years.
senses.exampleCN: 老妇人预言旱情会持续七年。
senses.why: The same act of speaking first, but the authority comes from revelation rather than from data.
senses.whyCN: 同样是先说出口的动作，只是权威来自启示而非数据。

senses.title: To expect or anticipate
senses.titleCN: 预料：心里已经先把它算上
senses.definition: to expect something to happen, often in everyday planning
senses.definitionCN: 预期某事会发生，常用于日常安排
senses.example: We predicted heavy traffic and left an hour early.
senses.exampleCN: 我们预料会堵车，所以提前一小时出发。
senses.why: Prediction need not be public. Private anticipation is the same forward-looking move, kept inside the head.
senses.whyCN: 预测不必公开。私下的预料是同一个朝前的动作，只是留在脑子里。

senses.title: Statistics: to estimate a value
senses.definition: to produce an estimated value for a future or unknown observation from a model
senses.definitionCN: 用模型为未来或未知的观测给出一个估计值
senses.example: The model predicts sales of 12,000 units in the first quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 模型预测第一季度销量为一万二千件。
senses.why: In statistics the prediction is a number with an interval, not a sentence. The verb becomes a technical operation.
senses.whyCN: 在统计学里，预测是一个带区间的数，而不是一句话。这个动词变成了一项技术操作。

senses.title: To warn in advance
senses.titleCN: 预告：提前提醒，好让人准备
senses.definition: to announce something in advance so that people can prepare for it
senses.definitionCN: 事先告知某事，以便人们可以准备
senses.example: The report predicted shortages and urged hospitals to stock up.
senses.exampleCN: 报告预告了短缺，并敦促医院囤货。
senses.why: Saying it early has a use: it buys time. Prediction becomes a warning when the future it names is unwelcome.
senses.whyCN: 提前说出来是有用的：它买来时间。当所命名的未来不受欢迎时，预测就成了预警。

intro.en: Predict is a Latin compound meaning to say beforehand. It is one of a large family built on the verb dicere, to say.
intro.cn: predict 是一个意为“事先说出”的拉丁复合词。它属于一个建立在动词 dicere（说）之上的大词族。

items.en: Dicere meant 'to say, declare'. It is the source of diction, dictionary, verdict, contradict, and predict.
items.cn: dicere 意为“说、宣告”。它是 diction、dictionary、verdict、contradict、predict 的来源。

items.en: Prae meant 'before, in front'. Joined to a verb of saying, it produces the sense of saying something before its time.
items.cn: prae 意为“在前”。与表示“说”的动词结合，就产生“在时间之前说出来”的意思。

items.en: Praedicere meant 'to make known beforehand, to declare in advance'. It was used for foretelling as well as for public proclamation.
items.cn: praedicere 意为“事先让人知道、预先宣告”。它既用于预言，也用于公开宣布。

items.en: The past participle praedictus meant 'foretold'. English keeps it inside words like prediction and predictably.
items.cn: 过去分词 praedictus 意为“被预言的”。英语把它保留在 prediction、predictably 这类词里。

items.en: English predict appears in the 16th century, at first in religious and learned writing about foretelling. The modern data-based sense develops much later.
items.cn: 英语 predict 出现于 16 世纪，最早见于谈论预言的宗教与学术写作。以数据为基础的现代义要晚得多才发展出来。

items.en: With the rise of science and statistics, predict becomes the standard word for evidence-based foretelling, while prophesy remains the religious term.
items.cn: 随着科学与统计的兴起，predict 成了“有据预告”的标准词，而 prophesy 保持宗教色彩。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin verb for saying. The second group collects words for foretelling, each with a different basis of authority.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语表示“说”的动词。第二组收表示“预告”的词，各自依据的权威不同。

entries.definition: a statement about what will happen. It is the noun built on predict with -ion.
entries.definitionCN: 关于将会发生什么的陈述。它是 predict 加 -ion 构成的名词。

entries.definition: able to be foreseen, often with a hint of dullness. Predict plus -able.
entries.definitionCN: 可以被预见的，常带一点乏味的暗示。predict 加 -able。

entries.definition: the part of a sentence that says something about the subject, or to base something on. It comes from Latin praedicare, a cousin of praedicere.
entries.definitionCN: 句子中陈述主语的部分，或“以……为依据”。它来自拉丁 praedicare，是 praedicere 的近亲。

entries.definition: a decision or judgement. Ver- 'true' plus dict 'said': what is said as true.
entries.definitionCN: 裁决或判定。ver-“真”加 dict“说”：被说成真实的话。

entries.definition: to say what is likely in weather, economics, or other systems. Forecast is common for weather and trends; predict is the general term.
entries.definitionCN: 预告天气、经济或其他系统的可能状况。forecast 多用于天气与趋势；predict 是一般用语。

entries.definition: to tell of a future event. Foretell is literary and often implies a sign or a seer.
entries.definitionCN: 讲述未来的事件。foretell 带文学色彩，常暗示有征兆或预言者。

entries.definition: to foretell under divine inspiration. Prophesy claims a religious authority that predict does not.
entries.definitionCN: 在神圣启示下预告未来。prophesy 主张一种宗教权威，predict 没有这种主张。

entries.definition: to expect something and often act in advance. Anticipate adds preparation; predict can be purely a statement.
entries.definitionCN: 预期某事并常提前行动。anticipate 多出“准备”之意；predict 可以只是陈述。

entries.definition: to estimate future figures from present trends. Project is technical and numerical, closer to sense 07.
entries.definitionCN: 由当前趋势估算未来数字。project 是技术性、数值性的，更接近第 7 义项。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks: the sentence said too early, the economist's model, the particle found later, the dark clouds, and the shopping list made before the rush.
normalIntro.cn: 五个抓手：提早说出的那句话、经济学家的模型、后来找到的粒子、乌云、以及抢购前先列好的清单。

normal.en: Pre- means before, dict means say. Predict is say-before.
normal.cn: pre- 是“在前”，dict 是“说”。predict 就是“先说”。

normal.en: A weather forecast and a stock forecast are both predict with numbers plugged in.
normal.cn: 天气预报和股市预测，都是把数字代进去的 predict。

normal.en: A theory predicts a particle, then the lab goes looking for it. Prediction is the theory's exam.
normal.cn: 理论预言一种粒子，实验室随后去找它。预测就是理论的那场考试。

normal.en: Dark clouds predict rain without saying a word: signs can also speak.
normal.cn: 乌云一言不发就预示下雨：迹象也会说话。

normal.en: Predicting a rush and leaving early is the same verb, just kept private.
normal.cn: 预料拥堵并提早出门，是同一个动词，只是留在心里。

abstract.en: Every prediction is a promise the present makes about the future, and it can be broken by a single unforeseen event.
abstract.cn: 每个预测都是现在对未来作出的承诺，而它可能被一个未预见的事件打破。

abstract.en: The difference between prophecy and prediction is not the content but the warrant: revelation versus evidence.
abstract.cn: 预言与预测的差别不在内容，而在凭据：是启示，还是证据。

abstract.en: To predict well is to be willing to be wrong in public, which is why science prizes it.
abstract.cn: 预测得好，意味着愿意在公众面前出错；正因如此，科学看重它。

examples.en: The model predicts that sea levels will rise by about half a metre this century.
examples.cn: 该模型预测本世纪海平面将上升约半米。

examples.en: As predicted, the first frost came in the last week of October.
examples.cn: 正如所料，初霜在十月最后一周到来。

examples.en: Analysts predict a sharp fall in demand for new cars.
examples.cn: 分析人士预测新车需求将大幅下降。

dict_mnemonic.text: “普瑞迪克特”——普瑞提前把“迪克特”那件事说出口，就是 predict（预测）

root: 拉丁语 praedicere“事先说出、预先宣告”＝prae“在前”+ dicere“说” → 英语 predict（16 世纪）；与 diction、dictionary、verdict、contradict 同根。

sensesIntro.en: The word always means saying something before it happens. What changes is the basis: evidence, theory, signs, revelation, private expectation, or a statistical model. Each basis gives a slightly different shade of the same forward-speaking act.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词始终指“在事情发生之前先说出来”。变化的是依据：证据、理论、征兆、启示、私下预期，或统计模型。每一种依据都给同一个“朝前说话”的动作一种不同的色调。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sentence spoken today about an event that has not yet arrived.
core.cn: 核心意象：今天说出一句话，说的是尚未到来的事件。

branches.en: SPEECH: saying or expecting, public or private.
branches.cn: 言语：说出或预料，公开或私下。

branches.en: CALCULATION: forecasts from data, and statistical estimates.
branches.cn: 计算：由数据作出的预报，以及统计估计。

branches.en: SCIENCE: the theory that names a result before it is observed.
branches.cn: 科学：在结果被观察之前就把它命名的理论。

branches.en: SIGN AND WARNING: the world speaking through evidence, and the early notice that buys time.
branches.cn: 征兆与预警：世界借证据说话，以及买来时间的提前告知。

branches.en: PROPHECY: the same act, warranted by revelation.
branches.cn: 预言：同一个动作，凭据是启示。

intro.en: Predict is one compound from the large dicere family. Every word below is either a piece of that compound or a sibling built with another prefix on the same verb of saying.
intro.cn: predict 是 dicere 大词族里的一个复合词。下面每个词，要么是这个复合词的构件，要么是在同一个“说”的动词上加别的前缀构成的兄弟词。

latinIntro.en: Latin praedicere and its participle praedictus supplied the English forms; the same dic- stem appears across law, grammar, and everyday speech.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 praedicere 及其分词 praedictus 提供了英语形式；同一个 dic- 词干出现在法律、语法与日常言语中。
