senses.title: Like one thing more than another
senses.definition: to like or want one thing more than another
senses.definitionCN: 比另一件东西更喜欢或更想要某一件
senses.example: She prefers tea to coffee.
senses.exampleCN: 比起咖啡，她更喜欢茶。
senses.why: Prae- means before and ferre means to carry, so the liked thing is carried in front of the other in one's esteem.
senses.whyCN: prae- 意为「在前」，ferre 意为「搬运」，被喜欢的那样东西于是被搬到另一样东西前面，排在心上更靠前的位置。

senses.title: Choose one option rather than the other
senses.definition: to choose one course or option rather than another because it suits one better
senses.definitionCN: 因为更合心意而选择一种做法或选项，而不是另一种
senses.example: We preferred to walk rather than wait for the bus.
senses.exampleCN: 我们宁愿走路，也不想等公交。
senses.why: Once one thing is placed in front, the hand follows it, so preference turns into a choice between courses of action.
senses.whyCN: 一样东西一旦被放到前面，手就会跟着它走，于是「更喜欢」变成了在几种做法之间的选择。

senses.title: Give precedence to a claim or method
senses.titleCN: 给予某项主张或方法优先地位
senses.definition: to treat one claim, method or person as more important than the others
senses.definitionCN: 把某项主张、方法或某个人看得比其他更重
senses.example: The committee preferred the cheaper design.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会更倾向于那个造价更低的方案。
senses.why: Ranking is placing in a row, and what is carried to the front of the row is what counts first.
senses.whyCN: 排序就是把东西排成一列，被搬到最前面的那一个，就是最先被考虑的那一个。

senses.title: Bring a charge or claim before a court
senses.titleCN: 向法庭提出控告或主张
senses.definition: to bring a charge, claim or request formally before a court or an authority
senses.definitionCN: 正式向法庭或主管机关提出控告、索赔或请求
senses.example: The prosecutor preferred charges of fraud against the firm.
senses.exampleCN: 检察官对这家公司提出了欺诈指控。
senses.why: Legal Latin kept the literal sense of bringing something forward, so a charge is carried before the bench.
senses.whyCN: 法律拉丁语保留了「把东西搬到前面」的字面意思，因此控告就是被搬到法官席前的东西。

senses.title: Advance someone to a higher office
senses.titleCN: 把某人提拔到更高的职位
senses.definition: to promote someone to a higher position or a more valuable office
senses.definitionCN: 把某人提升到更高或更优厚的职位
senses.example: The bishop was preferred to a wealthier see.
senses.exampleCN: 这位主教被提拔到一个更富裕的教区。
senses.why: A person raised above his peers is literally carried in front of them in rank.
senses.whyCN: 一个人被抬到同辈之上，在位次上就是被搬到了他们前面。

senses.title: Regard one explanation as more likely
senses.titleCN: 认为某一种解释更可能成立
senses.definition: to judge one explanation, reading or hypothesis as more likely than another
senses.definitionCN: 判断某一种解释、读法或假说比另一种更可能
senses.example: Historians prefer the simpler reading of the letter.
senses.exampleCN: 历史学家更认可对这封信较为简单的解读。
senses.why: The mind also carries things forward: among competing readings, one is placed ahead of the rest.
senses.whyCN: 心思也会搬东西：在几种相互竞争的解释里，总有一种被放到其余之前。

senses.title: Express a softer wish about another person's action
senses.titleCN: 委婉表达希望对方如何做
senses.definition: to say politely that one would rather have something done in a particular way
senses.definitionCN: 礼貌地表示自己更希望某事以某种方式进行
senses.example: I would prefer it if you called before coming.
senses.exampleCN: 我希望你来之前先打个电话。
senses.why: The comparative force softens a request: the speaker names a preferred arrangement instead of giving an order.
senses.whyCN: 比较的意味让请求变软：说话人只是说出更合意的安排，而不是下命令。

senses.title: Decide at one's own discretion
senses.titleCN: 按自己的判断自行决定
senses.definition: to decide according to one's own judgment, especially in formal rules that leave the choice open
senses.definitionCN: 按自己的判断作出决定，尤用于把选择权留给当事人的正式规则
senses.example: The trustee may, as he prefers, sell the land at auction.
senses.exampleCN: 受托人可以按自己的判断，以拍卖方式出售这块土地。
senses.why: The oldest sense of placing one thing before another survives as the freedom to put whichever course one likes first.
senses.whyCN: 「把某样东西放到前面」这个最古老的意思，在这里留存为「可以把中意的做法排在前面」的自由。

intro.en: Prefer comes through Old French from Latin praeferre, built on prae- meaning before and ferre meaning to carry or bear. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: prefer 经古法语来自拉丁语 praeferre，由 prae-「在前」与 ferre「搬运、承载」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Ferre meant to carry or bear, and its past participle latus stands behind English words such as relate and translate. Its older source is generally reconstructed as a root meaning to carry.
items.cn: ferre 意为「搬运、承载」，其过去分词 latus 支撑着 relate、translate 等英语词。它更早的来源通常被重构为一个表示「搬运」的词根。

items.en: Prae- meaning before plus ferre produced praeferre, to place or carry in front, and by extension to value one thing above another.
items.cn: 表示「在前」的 prae- 加 ferre 构成 praeferre，意为「放到前面、搬在前面」，并引申为把某物看得比另一物更重。

items.en: Old French preferer brought the verb into English in the late fourteenth century, at first in the sense of putting a person or thing before others.
items.cn: 古法语 preferer 在十四世纪后期把这个动词带入英语，最初指把人或物放到其他之前。

items.en: By the sixteenth century the verb named esteeming one thing above another, and legal usage used it for bringing a charge or request forward.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，这个动词已指看重某物胜过另一物，法律用语则用它表示把控告或请求呈到前面。

items.en: The everyday sense of liking one thing better than another settled in ordinary speech, while the legal and church senses stayed in specialized use.
items.cn: 「更喜欢某物」这一日常义在普通口语中固定下来，而法律与教会用语里的意思则留在专门场合。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first English citation is not fixed, and the deeper Indo-European root of ferre is a reconstructed form rather than a recorded word.
items.cn: 来源不确定：英语中最早的书证年代没有定论；ferre 更深的印欧语词根属重构形式，并非有记录的真实词形。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin verb ferre but differs in prefix; the second holds words for liking and picking that are close in use. One look-alike has a different origin.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁动词 ferre，只是前缀不同；第二组是用法相近的「喜爱、挑选」类词。其中有一个形似词来源不同。

entries.definition: Re- meaning back plus ferre: to carry a matter back to a source, hence to direct attention or consult.
entries.definitionCN: re-「向后」加 ferre：把某事带回源头，因而指指向某处或查阅。

entries.definition: Con- meaning together plus ferre: to bring matters together, hence to consult or to bestow.
entries.definitionCN: con-「共同」加 ferre：把事情带到一处，因而指商议或授予。

entries.definition: Dis- meaning apart plus ferre: to carry things in different directions, hence to be unlike.
entries.definitionCN: dis-「分开」加 ferre：把东西带向不同方向，因而指彼此不同。

entries.definition: From Old French poroffrir, built on offrir and Latin offerre meaning to bring before; it looks like prefer but the prefix and source differ.
entries.definitionCN: 来自古法语 poroffrir，由 offrir 与拉丁语 offerre「呈到面前」构成；它与 prefer 形似，但前缀与来源都不同。

entries.definition: To treat one person or option with special approval; it stresses approval rather than a comparison between two things.
entries.definitionCN: 带着特别的认可对待某个人或某种选项；它强调认可，而不是两物之间的比较。

entries.definition: To pick one option; prefer names the leaning, choose names the act.
entries.definitionCN: 挑出一个选项；prefer 命名的是倾向，choose 命名的是动作。

entries.definition: To make a choice, often in a formal or deliberate context; it does not carry the comparative force of liking one more than another.
entries.definitionCN: 作出选择，常用于正式或慎重的场合；它不带有「比另一物更喜欢」的比较意味。

entries.definition: The everyday verb for finding something pleasant; prefer adds a comparison with something else.
entries.definitionCN: 表示觉得某物令人愉快的日常动词；prefer 则加上了与另一物的比较。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real prefix, the real root, the real family and the phrases the verb keeps.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的前缀、真实的词根、真实的同族词，以及这个动词实际常用的搭配。

normal.en: prae- meaning before plus ferre meaning carry: to carry one thing in front of another.
normal.cn: prae-「在前」加 ferre「搬运」：把一样东西搬到另一样前面。

normal.en: The family runs prefer, preference, preferable, preferably, preferential and preferment.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 prefer（更喜欢）、preference（偏好）、preferable（更可取的）、preferably（更可取地）、preferential（优先的）、preferment（提拔）。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the comparison: prefer tea to coffee, prefer to wait, strongly prefer.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出比较关系：喜欢茶胜过咖啡、宁愿等待、强烈偏好。

normal.en: The same root runs through refer, confer, differ, infer and transfer, each with its own prefix.
normal.cn: 同一词根贯穿 refer、confer、differ、infer、transfer，各自配上不同的前缀。

normal.en: Legal usage keeps the old forward motion: to prefer charges is to bring them before a court.
normal.cn: 法律用法保住旧的「向前搬」动作：提出控告就是把控告呈到法庭前。

abstract.en: Picture two doors and a hand already resting on the right handle.
abstract.cn: 想象两扇门，一只手已经按在右边那扇的把手上。

abstract.en: Picture a clerk placing one file on top of a stack.
abstract.cn: 想象一名职员把一份卷宗放到整叠文件的最上面。

abstract.en: Picture a compass needle that always settles a little east of north.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚罗盘针，每次都停在正北略偏东的位置。

examples.en: Most readers prefer the shorter edition.
examples.cn: 多数读者更喜欢篇幅较短的版本。

examples.en: She preferred to say nothing until the facts were clear.
examples.cn: 在事实清楚之前，她宁愿什么都不说。

examples.en: The court preferred charges against two officers.
examples.cn: 法庭对两名警官提出了指控。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普瑞佛」——先把喜欢的那件捧到前面 → prefer 更喜欢、宁愿

root: 拉丁 praeferre「放到前面、看重」= prae-「在前」+ ferre「搬运、承载」；ferre 的印欧语来源通常被重构为表示「搬运」的词根。英语 prefer 经古法语进入。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one gesture: one thing is carried in front of another, and that placement is applied to taste, action, ranking, legal charges, offices, explanations, polite wishes and finally to open discretion.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：把一样东西搬到另一样前面，这个摆放再依次用于口味、行动、排序、法律控告、职位、解释、礼貌愿望，最后用于留有余地的自行裁量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two things offered side by side, and one is carried to the front of the hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：两样东西并排摆在面前，其中一样被搬到手上更靠前的位置。

branches.en: TASTE AND ACTION: the thing carried to the front is first liked, then taken.
branches.cn: 口味与行动：被搬到前面的东西先被喜欢，再被拿走。

branches.en: RANKING: precedence is the same placement seen as order rather than desire.
branches.cn: 排序：优先地位是同一种摆放，只是被看成次序而非喜好。

branches.en: FORMAL FORWARDING: a charge or a candidate is brought before the bench or above one's peers.
branches.cn: 正式呈交：控告或人选被带到法官席前，或被抬到同辈之上。

branches.en: READING: among explanations the mind puts one ahead of the rest.
branches.cn: 解读：在几种解释中，心思把其中一种放到其余之前。

branches.en: SOFTENED WILL: a polite wish and a formal discretion both leave the preferred course to the speaker.
branches.cn: 柔化的意愿：礼貌的愿望与正式的裁量，都把中意的做法留给说话人自己。

intro.en: Prefer can be read from a Latin prefix and a Latin verb that also build a large English family.
intro.cn: prefer 可以按一个拉丁前缀与一个拉丁动词逐段读出，这两部分还构成一大族英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin ferre gives refer, confer, differ, infer, transfer and prefer; prae- adds the sense of being in front.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ferre 衍生 refer、confer、differ、infer、transfer 与 prefer；prae- 加上「在前面」的意思。

items.example: The prefix also appears in predict and precede.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀也出现在 predict（预测）与 precede（在……之前）里。

items.example: Its participle latus underlies translate and relate.
items.exampleCN: 它的过去分词 latus 是 translate 与 relate 的词源基础。

items.meaning: to carry in front, hence to value more
items.exampleCN: 她更喜欢早一班的那趟车。

items.meaning: the state of liking one thing more
items.meaningCN: 偏好；更喜爱某物的状态
items.example: Her preference for quiet rooms is well known.
items.exampleCN: 她偏爱安静的房间，这是众所皆知的。

items.example: The earlier flight is preferable in winter.
items.exampleCN: 冬天早一班的航班更可取。

items.meaning: if the choice were open, in the better way
items.example: Bring cash, preferably in small notes.
items.exampleCN: 带上现金，最好是小面额的。

items.meaningCN: 优先的；给予一方优待的

items.meaning: an advance to a higher post
items.example: His preferment came after years of service.
items.exampleCN: 他在多年任职之后获得提拔。

items.structure: pro- + offerre (to bring before), a different formation
items.meaning: to hold out something for acceptance
items.exampleCN: 她递上一张手写的便条。

derivatives.structure: prefer + -ence (state) → the state of holding one thing above another
derivatives.meaning: a greater liking for one thing

derivatives.structure: prefer + -able (fit to be chosen) → fit to be chosen rather than the other
preferable + -ly (adverb) → in the more desirable way
prefer + -ential (relational adjective) → marked by giving advantage to one side
prefer + -ment (result) → the result of being raised above others

definition_zh: 准备；预备；使做好准备；配制；编写；筹备
definition_en: to make someone or something ready for what will happen, to put a dish or mixture together, or to draw up a plan or text
core_image: 案板上一排切好的菜，锅已烧热，手正把盐罐拉到近前
scene: 天还没亮，厨房的灯先亮了，她把米淘好放进锅里。She prepared a simple breakfast before the children woke.
sceneCN: 这里 prepare 是「配制、做好（饭菜）」（第 2 个义项：把食材做成可以吃的东西）；句意为她在孩子们醒来之前做好了一顿简单的早饭。图中可辨识物件：案板、切好的菜、热锅、盐罐。

pos.zh: 准备；预备；使做好准备；配制；编写

derivatives.zh: 由 prepare 换用名词后缀 -ation 构成，义为「准备；准备工作」
由拉丁词干 preparat- 加 -ory 构成，义为「预备的；筹备的」
由 prepare 加 -ed 构成，义为「有准备的；事先做好的」
由 prepared 加 -ness 构成，义为「有准备的状态；戒备」

senses.title: To get ready before something happens
senses.definition: to make yourself or something else ready for an event that is still to come
senses.definitionCN: 让自己或别的事物为尚未到来的事情进入就绪状态
senses.example: The team spent the morning preparing for the match.
senses.exampleCN: 队伍花了一上午为比赛做准备。
senses.why: Latin parare meant to make ready, and prae- adds the idea of doing it beforehand, so preparation is readiness produced in advance.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 parare 意为使就绪，prae- 又加上「事先」的意思，所以 preparation 就是提前造出来的就绪状态。

senses.title: To put a dish or mixture together
senses.definition: to combine ingredients and make them ready to eat or to use
senses.definitionCN: 把各种材料组合起来，做成可以吃或可以用的东西
senses.example: He prepared a pot of soup for the guests.
senses.exampleCN: 他为客人煮了一锅汤。
senses.why: Making a dish ready is the same act of putting things in order, so the verb moves from readiness in general to the kitchen without changing its core.
senses.whyCN: 把一道菜弄好，仍然是同样的「把东西整理到位」的动作，所以这个词从一般的就绪转到厨房，核心并没有变。

senses.title: To train or equip someone for a task
senses.definition: to give a person the knowledge or experience needed for a future task
senses.definitionCN: 让某人为将来的任务获得所需的知识或经验
senses.example: The course prepares students for work in a real lab.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课让学生为在真实实验室里工作做好准备。
senses.why: When the object is a person, readiness becomes training, and the verb names what teaching does before the test of real work.
senses.whyCN: 当宾语是人时，就绪就变成了训练，这个词命名的正是教学在真实工作检验之前所做的那一步。

senses.title: To draw up a text or plan
senses.definition: to write or compose a document, plan or set of figures in advance
senses.definitionCN: 提前写出或编写成文件、方案或一组数字
senses.example: She prepared a short report for the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 她为会议写了一份简短报告。
senses.why: A document is also made ready before it is used, which is why the verb covers drawing up papers as well as cooking.
senses.whyCN: 文件在使用之前同样要先被弄好，所以这个词既能指做饭，也能指起草文书。

intro.en: Prepare is a Latin verb of making ready with a prefix meaning beforehand, filtered through Old French, and English widened it to meals, lessons, reports and medicine.
intro.cn: prepare 是一个加上「事先」前缀的拉丁「使就绪」动词，经古法语传入，英语又把它扩展到饭菜、功课、报告与药物。

items.en: Parare meant to make ready, to furnish or to put something in order; its deeper origin is uncertain and is usually left open.
items.cn: parare 意为使就绪、置办或把东西整理好；它更早的来源不确定，一般认为难以定论。

items.en: Prae- means before, so praeparare meant to get something ready ahead of the moment it would be needed.
items.cn: prae- 意为「在……之前」，praeparare 便指在需要之前就把事情弄好。

items.en: The participle praeparatus, made ready, supplied adjective and noun forms that later languages reused.
items.cn: 分词 praeparatus 意为「已备好的」，后来的语言沿用了它提供的形容词与名词形式。

items.en: Old French kept the verb as preparer, and English borrowed it in the Middle Ages.
items.cn: 古法语把这个动词保留为 preparer，英语在中世纪将其借入。

items.en: Modern English widened prepare to meals, lessons, reports and medicine, all sharing the idea of readiness made in advance.
items.cn: 现代英语把 prepare 扩展到饭菜、功课、报告与药物，这些用法共享「提前备好」的意思。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms of the same Latin verb of readiness; the near-meaning group gathers verbs for getting things and people into position.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「使就绪」动词的形式；近义组收表示把事物与人安排到位的动词。

entries.definition: The act or process of getting ready, or a substance made ready for use.
entries.definitionCN: 由 prepare 转成的名词，指准备的过程，或配好的制剂。

entries.definition: Serving to get something ready, as in a preparatory course.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词根的形容词，义为预备的，如预科课程。

entries.definition: Ready, or made in advance rather than at the moment.
entries.definitionCN: 由 prepare 加 -ed 构成，义为有准备的、事先做好的。

entries.definition: To mend something; it comes from re- plus parare, to make ready again, so the root is shared but the meaning has moved.
entries.definitionCN: 同一词根的另一支，由 re- 加 parare（重新弄好）构成，词根相同但词义已转向修理。

entries.definition: To make something or someone completely prepared, used mostly in technical and military writing.
entries.definitionCN: 使完全就绪；多用于技术与军事文字。

entries.definition: To put things in a particular order or make plans for them.
entries.definitionCN: 安排；把事物按某种次序放好或作出计划。

entries.definition: To plan and put the parts of an activity into working order.
entries.definitionCN: 组织；把一项活动的各部分计划并安排妥当。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin verb of readiness with a prefix of time, and its family keeps returning to what is done before the moment of use.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是带时间前缀的拉丁「使就绪」动词，同族词反复回到「在使用之前先做好」这件事。

normal.en: Parare means to make ready, and prae- adds before, so prepare is literally to ready something beforehand.
normal.cn: parare 意为使就绪，prae- 加上「之前」，所以 prepare 字面上就是提前把某事弄好。

normal.en: Preparation is the noun from the same stem, naming the whole process rather than the single act.
normal.cn: preparation 是同一词干的名词，指整个过程，而不只是单个动作。

normal.en: Prepared can be an adjective, which is why we say someone is well prepared.
normal.cn: prepared 也可以作形容词，所以可以说某人有充分准备。

normal.en: Repair shares the same parare but with re-, to make ready again, and has drifted to mending.
normal.cn: repair 同样用 parare，但带 re-（重新弄好），词义已漂移到修理。

normal.en: Prepare a meal and prepare a report both mean putting parts in order before they are needed.
normal.cn: prepare a meal 与 prepare a report 都指在需要之前把各部分整理到位。

abstract.en: To prepare is to work in the present on behalf of a moment that has not arrived.
abstract.cn: 准备就是在当下为尚未到来的时刻做事。

abstract.en: The word assumes the future will ask something of you, and it answers before the question is spoken.
abstract.cn: 这个词假定未来会向你提出要求，并在问题说出口之前就先作答。

abstract.en: Cooking, teaching and writing all appear under one verb because all three are ways of arranging the world in advance.
abstract.cn: 做饭、教学与写作都归到同一个动词下，因为三者都是提前把世界安排好的方式。

examples.en: She prepared a simple breakfast before the children woke.
examples.cn: 她在孩子们醒来之前做好了一顿简单的早饭。

examples.en: The team spent the morning preparing for the match.
examples.cn: 队伍花了一上午为比赛做准备。

examples.en: The course prepares students for work in a real lab.
examples.cn: 这门课让学生为在真实实验室里工作做好准备。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扑瑞派」——先把人派到前面去等着；prepare 就是准备、预备。

root: 源自拉丁语 parare（使就绪、置办），加前缀 prae-（在前、事先）构成 praeparare，经分词 praeparatus 与古法语 preparer 进入英语；同族词有 preparation、preparatory，repair 亦出同一 parare。

sensesIntro.en: The core is readiness made in advance; the senses divide into general preparation, cooking, training people, and drawing up papers.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是提前造出的就绪状态；义项由此分出一般准备、做饭配药、训练人员，以及起草文书。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of chopped vegetables on a board, the pan already hot, a hand reaching for the salt.
core.cn: 核心意象：案板上一排切好的菜，锅已烧热，手正把盐罐拉到近前。

branches.en: a bag packed the night before a journey
branches.cn: 出发前一夜就收拾好的包

branches.en: vegetables cut and waiting beside a hot pan
branches.cn: 切好放在热锅旁的蔬菜

branches.en: a student practising on a lab bench before the test
branches.cn: 考试前在实验台上练习的学生

branches.en: a report laid on the table before the meeting starts
branches.cn: 会议开始前摆在桌上的报告

branches.en: a cook reading the recipe once before starting
branches.cn: 开火前先把菜谱看一遍的厨师

intro.en: The word is a Latin verb of readiness plus a prefix of time, and English added suffixes that turn it into a process, an adjective and a state.
intro.cn: 这个词是表示「使就绪」的拉丁动词加上时间前缀，英语又添上后缀，使它变成过程、形容词与状态。

latinIntro.en: Prepare goes back to Latin praeparare, from prae- and parare, to make ready; the participle praeparatus and the noun praeparatio carry the same stem.
latinIntro.cn: prepare 上溯拉丁语 praeparare，由 prae- 与 parare（使就绪）构成；分词 praeparatus 与名词 praeparatio 用的是同一词干。

definition_zh: 现在的；目前的；出席的；在场的；礼物；提出；呈现
definition_en: existing or happening now; being in a place; a gift; and to give, show, or put something before others
core_image: 一只手把东西伸到另一个人面前：此刻、此地、就在眼前
scene: 年会上，主持人把一个包装好的盒子递到老员工手里，全场鼓掌。The retiring engineer received a small present from the whole team.
sceneCN: 这里 present 是名词「礼物」（第 3 个义项：送给别人的东西）；句意为即将退休的工程师收到了全队送的一件小礼物。图中可辨识物件：包装盒、彩带、鼓掌的同事。

pos.zh: 现在的；目前的；出席的；在场的

derivatives.zh: 由 present 加 -ation 构成，义为「演示；陈述；颁发」
由 present 加 -ly 构成，义为「不久；目前」
由 present 加表示「做某事的人」的后缀 -er 构成，义为「主持人；演示者」
由 present 加 -able 构成，义为「拿得出手的；像样的」

senses.title: Existing or happening now
senses.definition: existing, happening, or being considered at this moment
senses.definitionCN: 此刻存在、发生或正在被考虑的
senses.example: The present situation calls for patience.
senses.exampleCN: 目前的形势需要耐心。
senses.why: Latin praesens describes what stands before the eyes, and what stands before the eyes is by definition what is here now.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 praesens 指「摆在眼前的」，而摆在眼前的东西按定义就是此刻的，所以这个词自然有了「现在的」义。

senses.title: Being in a place rather than absent
senses.definition: being in a particular place at a particular time
senses.definitionCN: 在某一时间身处某一地点
senses.example: All the members were present at the vote.
senses.exampleCN: 所有成员都出席了投票。
senses.why: The same participle can describe a person as well as a moment: whoever is before us is present in the room.
senses.whyCN: 同一个分词既能修饰时刻，也能修饰人：谁在我们眼前，谁就是「在场的」。

senses.title: A thing given to someone as a gift
senses.definition: something that you give to someone, especially on a special occasion
senses.definitionCN: 赠予某人的东西，尤指在特殊场合
senses.example: She wrapped the present in blue paper.
senses.exampleCN: 她用蓝纸把礼物包了起来。
senses.why: The noun came from the idea of something placed before a person, and a gift is exactly an object set in front of someone to be taken.
senses.whyCN: 名词来自「摆到某人面前的东西」这一想法，而礼物正是被放到对方面前、请对方收下的物件，义项由此固定下来。

senses.title: To offer or submit something formally
senses.definition: to give a plan, report, or proposal to someone in authority for them to consider
senses.definitionCN: 把计划、报告或建议正式交给有权者考虑
senses.example: She presented her proposal to the committee.
senses.exampleCN: 她向委员会提出了自己的方案。
senses.why: The Latin verb praesentare meant to place before someone; putting a document before a committee is the modern version of that gesture.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 praesentare 意为「放到某人面前」，把文件摆到委员会面前，就是这一动作在现代的版本。

senses.title: To show, display, or perform something
senses.definition: to show something to an audience, or to appear in a particular way
senses.definitionCN: 向观众展示某物，或以某种样子出现
senses.example: The theatre will present three new plays this spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这家剧院今年春天将上演三部新剧。
senses.why: Once you can place an object before people, you can also place a performance or an image before them, which is how the word reaches stages and screens.
senses.whyCN: 既然能把物件摆到人前，也就能把演出或形象摆到人前，于是这个词走上了舞台与屏幕。

intro.en: Present and presence come from the same Latin participle, but English moved the stress and stretched the meaning from being here to handing something over.
intro.cn: present 与 presence 出自同一个拉丁分词，但英语改变了重音位置，并把词义从「在这里」扩展到「把东西递过去」。

items.en: Prae- meant before or in front, and it marks whatever is put ahead of a person.
items.cn: prae- 意为「在前、在前面」，标示被放到某人面前的东西。

items.en: Esse was the verb to be, and its participle praesens described what is present or at hand.
items.cn: esse 是表示「存在」的动词，它的分词 praesens 描述「在场的、在手边的」东西。

items.en: The verb praesentare meant to place something before someone, and so to offer or show it.
items.cn: 动词 praesentare 意为把某物放到某人面前，因此引申为呈上、展示。

items.en: Old French kept both the adjective of being here and the verb of placing something before another person.
items.cn: 古法语同时保留了「在场的」形容词与「把东西放到别人面前」的动词。

items.en: English puts the stress on the first syllable for the adjective and noun, on the second for the verb, and the meanings spread from time and place to gifts and performances.
items.cn: 现代英语让形容词与名词重音落在第一音节、动词落在第二音节，词义则从时间与地点扩展到礼物与演出。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin participle of being before; the near-meaning group gathers words for gifts, current time, and being somewhere.
note.cn: 形近组共享表示「在眼前」的拉丁分词；近义组收礼物、当前时间与到场相关的词。

entries.definition: The state of being in a place.
entries.definitionCN: 在场的状态；出席。

entries.definition: A talk or display given to an audience.
entries.definitionCN: 向观众做的演示或展示。

entries.definition: Soon, or at this time.
entries.definitionCN: 不久；此刻。

entries.definition: To stand for something or speak for someone.
entries.definitionCN: 代表某物或替某人说话。

entries.definition: Something given to someone without payment.
entries.definitionCN: 无偿赠予他人的东西。

entries.definition: Happening or existing now.
entries.definitionCN: 现在发生或存在的。

entries.definition: To be at an event.
entries.definitionCN: 到场参加活动。

entries.definition: To give or propose something.
entries.definitionCN: 给予或提出某物。

normalIntro.en: One Latin participle gives both the thing that is here and the act of putting something in front of someone, and English separates them by stress.
normalIntro.cn: 一个拉丁分词同时给出「在这里的东西」与「把东西放到别人面前的动作」，英语用重音把两者分开。

normal.en: The adjective and noun stress the first syllable, the verb the second: PREZ-unt for a thing, pri-ZENT for an action.
normal.cn: 形容词与名词重音在第一音节，动词在第二音节：指物时读前重，指动作时读后重。

normal.en: Present and presence share the Latin participle praesens, so both begin with the idea of being before someone.
normal.cn: present 与 presence 共用一个拉丁分词，起点都是「在某人面前」。

normal.en: Present as a gift is the object placed before a person, the same gesture as presenting a report.
normal.cn: 作「礼物」的 present 是被放到人前的物件，与呈交报告是同一个动作。

normal.en: At present is a fixed phrase for this moment, built on the time sense of the adjective.
normal.cn: at present 是表示「此刻」的固定说法，建立在形容词的时间义上。

normal.en: Presentation and presenter add endings to the verb, naming the act and the person who performs it.
normal.cn: presentation 与 presenter 给动词加后缀，分别命名行为与执行的人。

abstract.en: One word holds a moment, a place, a gift and a stage, because all of them are put in front of someone.
abstract.cn: 一个词同时装下时刻、地点、礼物与舞台，因为它们都被摆到了某人面前。

abstract.en: The stress moves like the meaning: first syllable for what is here, second for what you do with it.
abstract.cn: 重音随词义移动：前重指「在这里的东西」，后重指「你拿它做什么」。

abstract.en: A present is only a present once it is handed over, which is why the noun and the verb share a shape.
abstract.cn: 礼物只有递出去才成为礼物，所以名词与动词共用一个形状。

examples.en: The present situation calls for patience.
examples.cn: 目前的形势需要耐心。

examples.en: She presented her proposal to the committee.
examples.cn: 她向委员会提出了自己的方案。

examples.en: He gave her a small present before leaving.
examples.cn: 他临走前送了她一件小礼物。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读起来像「pre（先）+ sent（送）」：先送到人前的是礼物，先摆到人前的是方案，present 就是「呈到面前」。

root: 拉丁语 prae-（在前）+ esse（存在）→ praesens（在眼前的），经古法语 present 进入英语；形容词与名词重音在第一音节，动词重音在第二音节。

sensesIntro.en: The core is something placed before someone: time and place first, then the gift put in front of a person, then the act of laying a plan or a show before others.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「摆到某人面前」：先是时间与地点上的「在眼前」，再是递到面前的礼物，最后是把方案或演出摆到别人面前。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an open hand holding something out toward another person.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把东西伸到另一个人面前。

branches.en: a clock showing this very minute
branches.cn: 钟面停在此刻这一分钟

branches.en: a full row of chairs with nobody missing
branches.cn: 一排椅子坐满，无人缺席

branches.en: a wrapped box held out with both hands
branches.cn: 双手递出的包装盒

branches.en: a folder laid on the committee table
branches.cn: 放在委员桌上的文件夹

branches.en: a curtain rising on a new play
branches.cn: 新戏开演时升起的幕布

intro.en: The word is a Latin participle of being, its verb of placing before, and the English endings that name the act, the person and the quality.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示「存在」的拉丁分词、表示「放到面前」的动词，以及命名行为、人物与性质的英语后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 总统；大学校长；董事长；会议主席
definition_en: the head of a state, a university, a company, or a meeting, especially one chosen to lead and to preside over others
core_image: 一张长桌的尽头，一个人坐在最前面的椅子上，所有人的目光都朝他那边
scene: 长桌两侧坐满了人，争论停不下来，最后大家都看向尽头那把椅子，等坐在那里的人开口。The president of the club called for a vote.
sceneCN: 这里 president 指「会长、会议主席」（第 4 个义项：被推举出来主持会议的人）；句意为俱乐部会长要求进行表决。图中可辨识物件：长桌、成排的椅子、举起的手。

collocations.phrase: the president of the United States

derivatives.zh: 由 president 换后缀 -cy 构成，义为「总统职位；任期」
由 president 加 -ial 构成，义为「总统的；总统制的」
与 president 同出拉丁 praesidere，义为「主持；担任主席」

senses.title: The head of a state
senses.definition: the elected head of a republic, who leads the government and represents the country
senses.definitionCN: 共和国的民选元首，领导政府并代表国家
senses.example: The president addressed the nation on television.
senses.exampleCN: 总统通过电视向全国发表讲话。
senses.why: The Latin source means to sit in front, and the leader of a state is pictured as the person seated at the head of the table where decisions are made.
senses.whyCN: 词源本义是「坐在前面」，国家领导人正被想象成长桌首位上坐着的人，所有决定都从他那里发出，因此「总统」是这个坐前意象在政治上的放大。

senses.title: The head of a university
senses.definition: the senior officer who leads a university or a college
senses.definitionCN: 领导一所大学或学院的最高负责人
senses.example: The president welcomed the new students at the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 校长在校门口迎接新生。
senses.why: A university is also a body with a council and a hall, so its leader inherits the same image of the person who sits before the assembly and speaks for it.
senses.whyCN: 大学同样有校务会议与礼堂，它的负责人也就继承了同一幅画面：坐在众人之前、代表整个机构讲话的人，于是这个词从国家元首平移到校长。

senses.title: The head of a company
senses.definition: the most senior officer of a company or organization
senses.definitionCN: 公司或机构中职位最高的负责人
senses.example: The president of the firm signed the contract.
senses.exampleCN: 公司董事长签署了这份合同。
senses.why: Boards meet around a table, and the officer who sits at its head and signs for the company keeps the literal seating arrangement inside the modern title.
senses.whyCN: 董事会围桌而坐，坐在首位、代表公司签字的那个人，把「坐前排」的字面安排原样保留在现代头衔里，因此同一个词也指董事长、总裁。

senses.title: The person who chairs a meeting
senses.definition: the person chosen to lead a meeting, a club, or an assembly
senses.definitionCN: 被推选出来主持聚会、俱乐部或集会的负责人
senses.example: The president of the club called for a vote.
senses.exampleCN: 俱乐部会长要求进行表决。
senses.why: This is the plainest surviving sense: the one who sits in front of the group, keeps order, and lets others speak in turn.
senses.whyCN: 这是最贴近字面的一个义项：坐在一群人前面、维持秩序、安排轮流发言的人；规模没有国家或公司那么大，却仍是「坐前排」的原样动作。

intro.en: President goes back to a Latin verb made of a prefix meaning in front and a verb meaning to sit; the title first named anyone who sat before a group, then the head of a state.
intro.cn: president 可追到由「在前」的前缀与「坐」的动词组成的拉丁语动词；这个头衔最初指坐在一群人前面的人，后来才指国家元首。

items.en: The prefix prae- meant before or in front, and it is the same element seen in many Latin words of rank and place.
items.cn: 前缀 prae- 意为「在前、在前面」，与许多表示位次和位置的拉丁词共用这一成分。

items.en: The verb sedere meant to sit, and it is the source of a wide family of English words about seats, sessions, and settling down.
items.cn: 动词 sedere 意为「坐」，派生出一大批关于座位、会议与安顿下来的英语词。

items.en: Praesidere joined the two: to sit before others, and therefore to watch over, guard, or lead an assembly.
items.cn: praesidere 把两者合起来：坐在别人前面，因此引申为看守、护卫、主持一个集会。

items.en: The present participle praesidens, with the stem praesident-, named the person who sits in front; this is the form English took.
items.cn: 现在分词 praesidens 的词干是 praesident-，指坐在前面的人，英语取用的正是这一形式。

items.en: Old French president passed the title into English, first for the officer of a meeting or a college, later for the head of a state and of a company.
items.cn: 古法语 president 把这个头衔传入英语，先指会议或学院的负责人，后来才指国家元首与公司最高负责人。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin verb for sitting in front; the near-meaning group gathers other titles for the person who leads a body.
note.cn: 形近组沿表示「坐在前面」的拉丁动词展开；近义组收其他称呼团体领导者的头衔。

entries.definition: To be in charge of a meeting or ceremony.
entries.definitionCN: 主持；担任会议或仪式的主席。

entries.definition: The office or the term of a president.
entries.definitionCN: 总统职位；任期。

entries.definition: Relating to a president or the office.
entries.definitionCN: 总统的；与总统职位有关的。

entries.definition: A standing committee that leads a larger body.
entries.definitionCN: 领导更大机构的常设委员会；主席团。

entries.definition: The person who leads a meeting or a committee.
entries.definitionCN: 主持会议或委员会的人；主席。

entries.definition: The head of a government, especially in some countries.
entries.definitionCN: 某些国家的政府首脑；总理。

entries.definition: The person in charge of a group or organization.
entries.definitionCN: 团体或机构的负责人。

entries.definition: The head of a school, especially in the United States.
entries.definitionCN: 尤指美国的学校校长。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin phrase turned into a title: the one who sits in front. Every sense keeps that seat at the head of the table.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是把一个拉丁短语变成头衔：「坐在前面的人」；每个义项都保留着长桌首位那把椅子。

normal.en: President is prae- plus sedere: the one who sits in front of the others.
normal.cn: president 是 prae- 加 sedere：坐在其他人前面的那个人。

normal.en: Preside is the verb underneath the title, and presidency names the office or the term.
normal.cn: preside 是头衔底下的动词，presidency 则指职位或任期。

normal.en: Presidential adds -ial to make the adjective, as in a presidential election.
normal.cn: presidential 加 -ial 构成形容词，例如 a presidential election（总统选举）。

normal.en: The same Latin verb gave presidium, a standing committee that also sits in front of a larger body.
normal.cn: 同一个拉丁动词也生出 presidium，指同样坐在更大机构前面的常设委员会。

normal.en: A club president and a company president share the title because both chair a body, not because both lead a country.
normal.cn: 俱乐部会长与公司董事长共用一个头衔，是因为两人都在主持一个团体，而不是因为两人都领导国家。

abstract.en: The oldest meaning is a seating plan: the person in the front chair gets to speak for everyone behind.
abstract.cn: 最古老的含义其实是一张座次表：坐在前面椅子上的人，替后面所有人说话。

abstract.en: Power in this word is drawn as a place at the table, which is why the same title fits a state, a school, and a firm.
abstract.cn: 这个词里的权力被画成「桌边的一个位置」，所以同一个头衔能装下国家、学校与公司。

abstract.en: Whenever a group needs one voice, it looks for someone to sit at the head of the table.
abstract.cn: 只要一个群体需要统一的声音，就会找一个人坐到长桌首位。

examples.en: The president addressed the nation on television.
examples.cn: 总统通过电视向全国发表讲话。

examples.en: The president of the university opened the ceremony.
examples.cn: 大学校长宣布典礼开始。

examples.en: She was elected president of the student union.
examples.cn: 她当选为学生会主席。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普瑞兹登特」——坐在最前面的人（pre- 在前，sid 坐），就是主席与总统；谐音只助记。

root: 拉丁语 prae-（在前）+ sedere（坐）→ praesidere（坐在前面、主持）→ 现在分词 praesidens（坐在前面的人）→ 古法语 president → 英语 president；字面就是「坐前排的人」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the seat at the front; the senses spread from chairing a small meeting to leading a university, a company, and a state.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「前排的座位」；义项从主持小会议，扩展到领导大学、公司与国家。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long table with one chair at its head and every face turned toward it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张长桌，尽头一把椅子，所有面孔都朝那边。

branches.en: a long table and one chair at its head
branches.cn: 一张长桌和尽头的一把椅子

branches.en: a hand raised to call for order
branches.cn: 举起要求安静的手

branches.en: a hall of freshmen waiting at the gate
branches.cn: 在校门口等候的新生

branches.en: a signature at the foot of a contract
branches.cn: 合同末尾的签名

branches.en: a broadcast from a desk to the whole country
branches.cn: 从办公桌后面传向全国的讲话

intro.cn: 这个头衔由拉丁前缀、表示「坐」的动词及其分词，再加上命名职位与性质的英语后缀构成。

definition_zh: 按；压；敦促；报刊；新闻界；出版社；榨取
definition_en: to push something firmly; to urge someone strongly; also newspapers and the people who produce them, a publishing house, or the act of squeezing juice or oil out
core_image: 一只手把按钮按到底，塑料外壳微微下陷，灯随即亮起
scene: 楼道里很暗，他伸出一根手指朝墙上的开关按下去，灯立刻亮起，脚步声也停了。Press the button twice if the door does not open.
sceneCN: 这里 press 指「按、压」（第 1 个义项：用手或工具对某物施加压力）；句意为如果门没开就按两次按钮。图中可辨识物件：墙上的开关、手指、走廊的灯。

derivatives.zh: 由 press 加名词后缀 -ure 构成，义为「压力」
由 press 加 -ing 构成，义为「紧迫的；迫切的」
由 pressure 加动词后缀 -ize 构成，义为「加压；密封加压」

senses.title: To push something firmly
senses.definition: to push steadily on something with the hand or a tool
senses.definitionCN: 用手或工具持续对某物施加推力
senses.example: Press the green button to start the machine.
senses.exampleCN: 按下绿色按钮启动机器。
senses.why: The Latin verb premere simply meant to press, and this physical push is the sense from which every other use of the word can be traced.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 premere 本义就是「压」，用手施加推力的这个动作是整个词义树的根，后面所有引申都能从这一下按压找到起点。

senses.title: To urge someone strongly
senses.definition: to try hard to persuade someone to do something, especially by repeating the request
senses.definitionCN: 反复请求以努力说服某人做某事
senses.example: The union pressed the government for a reply.
senses.exampleCN: 工会敦促政府给出答复。
senses.why: Pressure applied to a person rather than an object becomes insistence, so the same verb moves from pushing a surface to pushing a decision forward.
senses.whyCN: 把压力从物体转到人身上，就变成了「不断施压、要求答复」，按压的动作没有变，只是受力的对象从按钮变成了决策者，因此产生「敦促」这一义。

senses.title: Newspapers and the people who make them
senses.definition: newspapers and magazines as a group, together with the journalists who work for them
senses.definitionCN: 报纸与杂志这一整体，以及为其工作的记者
senses.example: The story was widely reported in the press.
senses.exampleCN: 这件事在新闻界被广泛报道。
senses.why: When printing presses made daily papers possible, the machine that pressed ink onto paper gave its name to the papers themselves and then to the whole profession.
senses.whyCN: 印刷机让日报成为可能，把油墨压到纸上的那台机器就用 press 来称呼，随后这个词从机器转到印出来的报纸，再扩指整个新闻行业。

senses.title: A publishing house
senses.definition: a company that prints and publishes books, or the business of publishing
senses.definitionCN: 印刷并出版书籍的公司，或出版这一行业
senses.example: The book came out under a small university press.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书由一家小型大学出版社出版。
senses.why: The same machine also names the firm that owns it, so press shifts from the equipment to the business that turns manuscripts into bound books.
senses.whyCN: 同一台机器也能代指拥有它的机构，于是 press 从设备滑向企业，用来指把书稿变成成书的出版社，这一义项至今保留在大学社名与出版品牌里。

senses.title: To squeeze out liquid
senses.definition: to squeeze fruit, seeds, or oil to get the liquid inside
senses.definitionCN: 挤压果实、种子或油料以取得其中的液体
senses.example: They press the olives within a day of picking.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在采摘当天就把橄榄榨成油。
senses.why: Squeezing olives is the most literal kind of pressing, force applied until something flows out, and it survives beside the abstract senses.
senses.whyCN: 榨橄榄是最字面的一种「压」：一直加力，直到有东西流出来；这个用法与引申义长期并存，说明表示压力的词始终保留着「压出液体」的具体一面。

intro.en: Press comes from a Latin verb for pressing; a repeated-action form of it reached French and then English, and the printing machine later pushed the word into newspapers and publishing.
intro.cn: press 来自表示「压」的拉丁动词；它的反复体形式经法语进入英语，后来印刷机又把这个词推进报刊与出版领域。

items.en: The verb premere meant to press, squeeze, or push down, and it is the base of a large family of English words.
items.cn: 动词 premere 意为压、挤、向下推，是一大批英语词的共同基础。

items.en: A frequentative form pressare described pressing again and again, and this is the branch that travelled into French.
items.cn: pressare 是反复体形式，表示「一再压」，进入法语的正是这一支。

items.en: Old French presser kept both the physical sense and the sense of urging someone, and English borrowed it as pressen.
items.cn: 古法语 presser 同时保留「压」的具体义与「催促某人」的引申义，英语借入后写作 pressen。

items.en: Middle English press covered pushing, crowding, and the machine that pressed ink onto paper.
items.cn: 中古英语的 press 覆盖推、挤，以及把油墨压到纸上的机器。

items.en: Modern English lets the noun name the machine, the newspapers it produces, the publishing house, and the journalists as a body.
items.cn: 现代英语让这个名词同时指机器、机器印出的报纸、出版社，以及作为群体的新闻工作者。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin root for pressing and its English compounds; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of force and words for the news industry.
note.cn: 形近组沿表示「压」的拉丁词根及其英语复合词展开；近义组收施加力量的动词与新闻行业的说法。

entries.definition: A steady force acting on a surface, or strong influence on a person.
entries.definitionCN: 持续作用在表面上的力；对人所施的压力。

entries.definition: Needing attention right away.
entries.definitionCN: 需要立刻处理的；紧迫的。

entries.definition: To press things together into a smaller space.
entries.definitionCN: 把东西压到一起，使其占更小空间。

entries.definition: To put a thought into words, or to send something fast.
entries.definitionCN: 把想法说出来；快速送出。

entries.definition: To move something away by force.
entries.definitionCN: 用力把某物推开。

entries.definition: To press something from both sides.
entries.definitionCN: 从两侧挤压某物。

entries.definition: Newspapers, television, and other channels of news.
entries.definitionCN: 报纸、电视等新闻传播渠道。

entries.definition: To ask strongly that something be done.
entries.definitionCN: 强烈要求做某事。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin verb of pressing plus its repeated form; the family spreads from physical force to urging people and to printing words on paper.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是表示「压」的拉丁动词及其反复体；词族从物理的力，扩展到催促人，再扩展到把字印到纸上。

normal.en: Press comes from Latin premere, to press, and its frequentative pressare gave the French verb that English borrowed.
normal.cn: press 来自拉丁语 premere（压），它的反复体 pressare 生出法语动词，再传入英语。

normal.en: Pressure is press plus -ure, the result of pressing: a force that keeps acting on a surface.
normal.cn: pressure 是 press 加 -ure，指压出来的结果：持续作用在表面上的力。

normal.en: Compress and express both keep the Latin root premere, one pressing things together, the other pressing ideas out.
normal.cn: compress 与 express 都保留拉丁词根 premere：一个把东西压到一起，一个把想法压出来。

normal.en: The printing press pressed ink into paper, and from that machine came the sense newspapers and journalists.
normal.cn: 印刷机把油墨压进纸里，而「报刊、记者」这一义正是从那台机器来的。

normal.en: Pressing as an adjective keeps the physical weight: a pressing problem is one that bears down on you now.
normal.cn: 形容词 pressing 保留了物理上的重量：a pressing problem 就是此刻压在你身上的问题。

abstract.en: Press is what force looks like when it has a direction: down on a button, out through an olive, or straight at a person who must answer.
abstract.cn: press 就是力有了方向之后的样子：向下按按钮，向外榨橄榄，或直直压向一个必须答复的人。

abstract.en: One machine that pushed ink into paper was enough to rename an entire profession.
abstract.cn: 一台把油墨压进纸里的机器，就足以给整个行业改名。

abstract.en: The word shows that persuasion and printing are both forms of applied pressure, one on people and one on surfaces.
abstract.cn: 这个词说明说服与印刷都是「加压力」的形式：一个作用在人身上，一个作用在表面上。

examples.en: Press the green button to start the machine.
examples.cn: 按下绿色按钮启动机器。

examples.en: The story was widely reported in the press.
examples.cn: 这件事在新闻界被广泛报道。

examples.en: She pressed the olives by hand.
examples.cn: 她用手把橄榄榨成油。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普雷斯」——手掌往下一「压」，就是 press；压出来的报纸也叫 press。谐音只助记。

root: 拉丁语 premere（压）→ 反复体 pressare（一再压）→ 古法语 presser → 中古英语 pressen → 英语 press；从「按压」引申出「施压敦促」，再由印刷机引申出「报刊、新闻界、出版社」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is downward force; the senses divide into physical pressing, pressure on people, squeezing out liquid, and the printing machine with everything it produced.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是向下的力；义项由此分为物理按压、对人施压、榨出液体，以及印刷机及其产物。

core.cn: 核心意象：一根手指把按钮按到底，灯以亮起作为回应。

branches.cn: 手指把按钮按到底

branches.cn: 橄榄油流进罐子

branches.cn: 桌上反复递上的请求

branches.en: a folded newspaper on a breakfast table

branches.cn: 书末页上的出版标记

intro.en: The word is a Latin verb of pressing, its repeated form, the French verb taken from it, and the English endings that name the force and the action.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示「压」的拉丁动词、其反复体、由它而来的法语动词，以及命名压力与动作的英语后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_en: the force pressing on a surface per unit area; also the feeling of strain, or the act of urging someone to do something

scene: 潜水员下潜到十米深处，耳膜被水压压得发紧，呼吸也变得费力。The pressure on the diver's mask increased with every metre of descent.
sceneCN: 这里 pressure 指「单位面积上所受的力」（第 1 个义项：压力、压强）；句意为每下潜一米，潜水员面罩所受的压力就增加。图中可辨识物件：潜水员、面罩、深度绳、气泡；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: Force per unit area
senses.definition: the force acting on a surface divided by the area of that surface
senses.definitionCN: 作用在表面上的力除以该表面的面积
senses.example: Pressure on the diver's mask increased with every metre of descent.
senses.exampleCN: 每下潜一米，潜水员面罩所受的压力就增加。
senses.why: Latin pressura named a pressing, and physics gave the word a precise ratio of force to area.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 pressura 本指「压」，物理学给了这个词「力与面积之比」的精确含义。

senses.title: Pressure in a gas or liquid
senses.definition: the internal pressure of a fluid, measured in pascals or bar
senses.definitionCN: 流体的内部压强，以帕或巴计
senses.example: The gas pressure in the cylinder doubled when it was heated.
senses.exampleCN: 钢瓶受热时，瓶内气体压强翻倍。
senses.why: fluids push outward in all directions, and the word measures that push.
senses.whyCN: 流体会向各个方向推，这个词测的就是这种推力。

senses.title: Blood pressure
senses.definition: the force with which blood presses against the walls of the arteries
senses.definitionCN: 血液对动脉壁施加的力
senses.example: His blood pressure rose during the climb.
senses.exampleCN: 他在攀登过程中血压升高。
senses.why: medicine applied the physical word to the body's own plumbing.
senses.whyCN: 医学把这个物理词用到人体自身的管道上。

senses.title: Psychological strain
senses.definition: the mental strain produced by demands that seem to exceed one's capacity
senses.definitionCN: 由似乎超出承受能力的要求造成的心理紧张
senses.example: The pressure of the final week kept her awake.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一周的压力让她睡不着。
senses.why: something weighing on the mind behaves like a weight on a surface, so the physical word serves feeling too.
senses.whyCN: 压在心头的东西行为像压在表面上的重量，于是物理词也服务感受。

senses.title: Social pressure
senses.definition: the influence of a group that pushes a person toward a particular choice
senses.definitionCN: 群体推动个人做出某种选择的影响
senses.example: Peer pressure made the younger students hide their doubts.
senses.exampleCN: 同伴压力让年纪较小的学生藏起自己的疑虑。
senses.why: a group can press on a person as steadily as a hand on a table.
senses.whyCN: 群体能像按在桌上的手一样，稳稳地压住一个人。

senses.title: The act of urging
senses.definition: the act of repeatedly urging or persuading someone to act
senses.definitionCN: 反复催促或说服某人采取行动的行为
senses.example: The committee applied pressure until the report was released.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会不断施压，直到报告被公布。
senses.why: pressing someone is the literal action of the Latin verb, carried into social life.
senses.whyCN: 催促某人正是那个拉丁动词的字面动作进入社会生活。

senses.title: The burden of demands
senses.titleCN: 工作与时间的紧迫负担
senses.definition: the weight of urgent work, deadlines or expectations
senses.definitionCN: 紧急工作、截止期限或期待带来的重负
senses.example: The staff worked under constant pressure during the season.
senses.exampleCN: 旺季期间员工一直在压力下工作。
senses.why: time and tasks can also pile up like a physical load.
senses.whyCN: 时间与任务也会像实物一样堆积起来。

senses.title: A weather system
senses.definition: a region of high or low atmospheric pressure shown on a weather map
senses.definitionCN: 天气图上标出的高压或低压区域
senses.example: A deep low pressure system crossed the coast overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 一个深厚的低压系统一夜之间越过海岸。
senses.why: meteorology uses pressure as the variable that organises the whole map.
senses.whyCN: 气象学把气压当作组织整张天气图的变量。

intro.en: Pressure comes through Old French from Latin pressura 'a pressing', a noun from premere 'to press, squeeze'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: pressure 经古法语来自拉丁 pressura「压、挤压」，它是 premere「压、挤」的名词形式。年代均为约数。

items.en: Premere meant 'to press, squeeze, hold down'; its past participle pressus lies behind the noun and the English verb press.
items.cn: premere 意为「压、挤、按住」，其过去分词 pressus 是名词与英语动词 press 的来源。

items.en: Pressura 'a pressing, pressure' was formed from the participle and used for the act and its result.
items.cn: pressura「压、挤压」由分词构成，既指动作也指结果。

items.en: Old French pressure and Latin pressura gave English pressure in the late fourteenth century, first meaning anguish or the act of pressing.
items.cn: 古法语 pressure 与拉丁 pressura 在十四世纪末给出英语 pressure，最初指痛苦或按压的动作。

items.en: The force-per-area sense is recorded from the seventeenth century, when experiments on air and fluids needed a precise term.
items.cn: 单位面积受力的物理义从十七世纪有记录，当时对空气与流体的实验需要一个精确术语。

items.en: Blood pressure appears in the eighteenth century, while the figurative senses of urgency and coercion grow from the same idea of something weighing down.
items.cn: 血压的用法出现在十八世纪，而紧迫与催逼的比喻义都从「有东西压下来」这一想法生长出来。

items.en: First English dates approximate: the earliest English use is usually dated to the late fourteenth century and the first physics citation to the seventeenth, though neither date is exact.
items.cn: 首见年代为约数：英语最早用法通常定在十四世纪末，最早的物理书证定在十七世纪，但两者都不确切。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the same verb that are not the noun; group two holds nouns for force, strain and tension.
note.cn: 第一组是同一动词来的形式、却不是这个名词；第二组是表示力、紧张与张力的名词。

entries.definition: The verb means to push down; as a noun it means the printing machines or the news media, not force per area.
entries.definitionCN: 动词意为向下按；作名词指印刷机或新闻界，而非单位面积上的力。

entries.definition: To keep the air in a cabin or tank at a chosen pressure; it acts on a space, not on a person's mind.
entries.definitionCN: 让机舱或容器中的空气保持某一压强；作用于空间，不作用于人的心理。

entries.definition: As an adjective it means urgent; as a noun it means an act of ironing or a batch of records.
entries.definitionCN: 作形容词意为紧迫的；作名词指熨烫动作或一批唱片。

entries.definition: Describing someone who is subjected to pressure; it is not the noun itself.
entries.definitionCN: 形容承受压力的人；并非名词本身。

entries.definition: A broader word for strain on a person or material; pressure is the force, stress is often the response.
entries.definitionCN: 指人或材料所受紧张的更宽泛词；pressure 偏力，stress 常指反应。

entries.definition: The deformation or damage caused by a load; it describes the effect rather than the pushing force.
entries.definitionCN: 载荷造成的变形或损伤；描述结果，而非推力。

entries.definition: A pulling force along a rope or a nervous stretch; the opposite direction from pressure.
entries.definitionCN: 沿绳的拉力或神经上的紧绷；方向与压力相反。

entries.definition: A push or pull without reference to area; pressure is force divided by area.
entries.definitionCN: 不涉及面积的推或拉；pressure 是力除以面积。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real word parts, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin premere 'press' gives press, pressure, pressurize, pressing.

normal.en: Physics defines it as force divided by area; the unit is the pascal.
normal.cn: 物理学把它定义力除以面积，单位是帕。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the senses: under pressure, blood pressure, high pressure.
normal.cn: 固定搭配区分义项：在压力之下、血压、高压。

normal.en: The same word serves a diver's mask, a hospital ward and a committee room.
normal.cn: 同一个词服务潜水员的面罩、医院病房与委员会会议室。

normal.en: A weather map is drawn in pressure, with highs and lows.
normal.cn: 天气图以气压绘制，标出高压与低压。

abstract.en: Picture a palm flat on a table, the weight spread across the whole contact.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手掌平放在桌上，重量摊在整个接触面。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd leaning toward one person until that person moves.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人向一个人倾压过去，直到那人让步。

abstract.en: Picture a column of water above a small mask, growing heavier metre by metre.
abstract.cn: 想象一小块面罩上方的水柱，一米一米地变重。

examples.en: The pressure inside the tank was too high for the valve.
examples.cn: 罐内压力对阀门来说过高。

examples.en: She felt the pressure of the deadline all week.
examples.cn: 她整个星期都感到截止期的压力。

examples.en: A low pressure system brought rain to the coast.
examples.cn: 一个低压系统给沿海带来降雨。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one pressing force: the physical quantity, the pressure inside a fluid, blood pressure, mental strain, group pressure, the act of urging, the burden of urgent work and finally a weather system.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种压下的力展开：物理量、流体内压、血压、心理紧张、群体压力、催逼的动作、紧迫工作的重负，最后是一个天气系统。

senses.title: Attractive to look at
senses.definition: Attractive to look at
senses.definitionCN: 好看、悦目的
senses.example: She wore a pretty dress to the party.
senses.exampleCN: 她穿了一条漂亮的裙子去聚会。
senses.why: Pretty is a shortened form of Old English prættig, which meant clever or crafty; by Middle English the word had shifted to pleasing to the eye.
senses.whyCN: pretty 是古英语 prættig（机灵、狡猾）的缩略形式，中古英语时词义已转为悦目好看。

senses.title: To a fairly high degree
senses.definition: To a fairly high degree
senses.definitionCN: 程度颇高，但不走极端
senses.example: The test was pretty easy.
senses.exampleCN: 这次测验相当容易。
senses.why: The adjective meaning pleasing weakened into an adverb of degree: what is pretty good is good enough to please.

definition_zh: 阻止；防止；使无法；妨碍；预防
definition_en: to stop something from happening, or to make it impossible for someone to do something
core_image: 有人还没走到门口，一条手臂已经横在门框上把路挡住
scene: 雨天路滑，小区门口新铺了一道减速带，旁边立着一块提示牌。The speed bump was installed to prevent accidents at the gate.
sceneCN: 这里 prevent 是「预防、防止发生」（第 3 个义项：采取措施，使事故一类的事不发生）；句意为这道减速带是为了防止门口发生事故而设。图中可辨识景物：减速带、雨后的路面、提示牌。

pos.zh: 使某人无法做某事；妨碍

derivatives.zh: 由 prevent 加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「阻止；预防」
由 prevent 加 -ive 构成，义为「预防的；防护的」
由 prevent 加 -able 构成，义为「可预防的；可以避免的」

senses.title: To stop an event from taking place
senses.definition: to stop an event or action before it can happen
senses.definitionCN: 使某个事件或行动来不及发生
senses.example: Quick action prevented a serious fire.
senses.exampleCN: 迅速的行动阻止了一场严重的火灾。
senses.why: Latin praevenire meant to come before someone; arriving at a place first is what lets you stand in the way of what follows.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 praevenire 意为「先于某人到来」，先一步赶到某处，才有机会挡在后头那件事的前面，所以「阻止」是「先来」的直接结果。

senses.title: To make it impossible for someone to act
senses.titleCN: 使某人无法做某事；妨碍
senses.definition: to make it impossible for someone to do what they intended
senses.definitionCN: 使某人无法做成原本打算做的事
senses.example: The storm prevented us from leaving the island.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨使我们无法离开这座岛。
senses.why: Here no force is aimed at the person; the word only reports that an obstacle got there first and the action never began.
senses.whyCN: 这里并不对某人施加力量，只是说明障碍先到了，那个动作始终没能开始，所以介词 from 后面接的是被挡住的行动。

senses.title: To reduce the risk of illness or damage
senses.definition: to take action so that illness, damage, or trouble does not develop
senses.definitionCN: 采取措施，使疾病、损害或麻烦不致发展起来
senses.example: Washing your hands helps prevent the spread of infection.
senses.exampleCN: 勤洗手有助于预防感染扩散。
senses.why: Medicine widened the focus from one event to a whole class of risk: acting early becomes a habit rather than a single block in a doorway.
senses.whyCN: 医学把焦点从单一事件扩大成一整类风险：提前动手变成习惯，而不再是门口一次性的拦阻，于是「预防」从「阻止」里独立出来。

senses.title: To go before, in older religious language
senses.definition: to go before or act ahead of someone, a sense kept mainly in old prayers
senses.definitionCN: 走在某人之前或先行行动，这一义项主要保留在古老祷词中
senses.example: The old prayer asks God to prevent us in all our doings.
senses.exampleCN: 那篇古老祷词祈求上帝在我们一切所行的事上先行引导。
senses.why: This is the literal Latin meaning surviving in English; modern usage narrowed the word, but the prayer book never changed.
senses.whyCN: 这是拉丁语本义在英语里的遗留：字面上就是「走在前面」。现代用法把词义收窄了，祷词却一直没改，所以这个古老义项仍能读到。

intro.en: Prevent is built from a Latin prefix meaning before and the verb to come: to prevent is, quite literally, to get there first, and hindering grew out of that head start.
intro.cn: prevent 由表示「在前」的拉丁前缀与动词「来」构成：字面上就是「先到一步」；阻挡的义项，正是从这个抢先到达的动作长出来的。

items.en: Prae- meant before or in front, the same prefix that appears in predict and prepare.
items.cn: prae- 意为「在前、在……前面」，predict 与 prepare 也用了这个前缀。

items.en: Venire meant to come, and it supplies the ven- seen in intervene, convene and event.
items.cn: venire 意为「来」，intervene、convene、event 里的 ven- 都来自它。

items.en: Praevenire meant to come before someone, to arrive ahead of them, and so to anticipate or forestall.
items.cn: praevenire 意为「先于某人来到」，即赶在对方前头到达，因此引申为预先、抢先拦下。

items.en: Old French prevenir kept both the sense of arriving first and the sense of hindering by getting there early.
items.cn: 古法语 prevenir 同时保留「先到」与「因先到而阻挡」两层意思。

items.en: Modern English dropped the literal meaning and kept the result: something is prevented when it never gets to happen.
items.cn: 现代英语丢掉了字面上的「先到」，只留下结果：一件事始终没能发生，就是被 prevent 了。

note.cn: 形近组沿着拉丁语中表示「来」的动词展开；近义组收阻挡、避开与消解祸患的动词。

normalIntro.en: The word puts a Latin prefix meaning before onto the verb to come, and its family keeps the picture of arriving first.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词在表示「来」的拉丁动词前加上「在前」的前缀，同族词都保留着「先一步到达」的画面。

normal.en: Prae- plus venire: prevent is to come before, and only later to block because you got there first.
normal.cn: prae- 加 venire：prevent 本是「先来」，后来才因先到而挡住。

normal.en: The ven- of prevent means come, as in invent and convene; pretend has a different verb, tendere, meaning stretch, so the two share only the prefix.
normal.cn: prevent 里的 ven- 意为「来」，invent、convene 同此；pretend 用的是另一个动词 tendere（伸展），两词只共享前缀，词源并不相同。

normal.en: Prevention is the noun and preventive the adjective; both name stopping something ahead of time.
normal.cn: prevention 是名词，preventive 是形容词，两者都指提前挡住。

normal.en: Preventable marks what can be stopped, with the same -able heard in avoidable and curable.
normal.cn: preventable 标注「拦得住的」，后缀 -able 与 avoidable、curable 里的相同。

normal.en: The pattern「prevent somebody from doing something」keeps the image of a body standing in another person's way.
normal.cn: 搭配「prevent somebody from doing something」保留了「一个人挡在另一个人路上」的画面。

abstract.en: To prevent is to win a race nobody watches: the best prevention leaves nothing to see afterwards.
abstract.cn: prevent 是赢下一场没人观看的比赛：最好的预防，事后什么也看不见。

abstract.en: The word once meant arrive first, and every act of prevention is still a small race against an event.
abstract.cn: 这个词原本只表示「先到」，而每一次预防，仍是在和某个事件抢时间。

abstract.en: Prevent and pretend share a prefix but not a road: one comes first, the other stretches a screen.
abstract.cn: prevent 与 pretend 共享前缀，却不同路：一个抢先赶到，一个撑起帘子。

examples.en: Quick action prevented a serious fire.
examples.cn: 迅速的行动阻止了一场严重的火灾。

examples.en: The storm prevented us from leaving the island.
examples.cn: 暴风雨使我们无法离开这座岛。

examples.en: Washing your hands helps prevent the spread of infection.
examples.cn: 勤洗手有助于预防感染扩散。

senses.title: The money asked for a good
senses.definition: the amount of money a seller asks for an item or service
senses.definitionCN: 卖方为某件商品或服务索要的金额
senses.example: The price of the coat was reduced twice before it sold.
senses.exampleCN: 这件外套的价格降了两次才卖出去。
senses.why: the core sense is a stated amount, which is what a price tag shows.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是一个被标出的金额，也就是价签所显示的内容。

senses.title: What must be given up
senses.titleCN: 为得到某物必须付出的代价
senses.definition: the cost in effort, risk or lost alternatives of obtaining something
senses.definitionCN: 为获得某物而在努力、风险或放弃的其他选择上付出的代价
senses.example: The price of success was three years without weekends.
senses.exampleCN: 成功的代价是三年没有周末。
senses.why: the word extends from money to any scarce thing given up, because both are what one pays.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从金钱延伸到任何被放弃的稀缺之物，因为两者都是所付出的东西。

senses.title: To set a price on something
senses.definition: to decide and mark the amount to be charged for an item
senses.definitionCN: 决定并标出某项商品的收费金额
senses.example: They priced the tickets at twenty pounds.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把票价定为二十英镑。
senses.why: the verb is the noun turned into an act of assigning the amount.
senses.whyCN: 动词是名词转为「指派金额」的动作。

senses.title: The general level of prices
senses.definition: the average level of charges across an economy at a given time
senses.definitionCN: 某一时期一个经济体中收费的平均水平
senses.example: Prices rose faster than wages for a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 有十年时间，物价涨得比工资快。
senses.why: in the plural the word often means the general level rather than one tag.
senses.whyCN: 用复数时，这个词常指总体水平，而非一张价签。

senses.title: A reward offered for a capture
senses.titleCN: 为缉拿或寻回而设的赏金
senses.definition: a sum offered to anyone who finds a person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 向找到某人或某物者提供的金额
senses.example: A price was put on the fugitive's head.
senses.exampleCN: 有人为这名逃犯的人头设了赏金。
senses.why: the older sense treats a reward as the amount paid for a result.
senses.whyCN: 较旧的义项把赏金看作「为某个结果所付的金额」。

senses.title: A quoted buying or selling rate
senses.definition: the rate at which a dealer will buy or sell in a financial market
senses.definitionCN: 交易商在金融市场愿意买进或卖出的价位
senses.example: The bond price fell after the announcement.
senses.exampleCN: 公告之后债券价格下跌。
senses.why: financial markets quote two prices, a bid and an offer, so the noun names a rate rather than a tag.
senses.whyCN: 金融市场报出买价与卖价两个价位，因此这个名词指一个比率，而非标签。

senses.title: Odds in racing or betting
senses.definition: the odds offered on a horse or outcome, expressed as a price
senses.definitionCN: 对某匹马或某个结果开出的赔率，以价位表示
senses.example: The bookmaker shortened the price on the favourite.
senses.exampleCN: 博彩商调低了热门马匹的赔率。
senses.why: betting calls odds a price because the stake buys a chance at a return.
senses.whyCN: 博彩把赔率称作 price，因为赌注买到的是一次回报机会。

senses.title: Any scale of worth
senses.titleCN: 衡量与交换的价值尺度（抽象义）
senses.definition: the measure by which a society or person values something
senses.definitionCN: 社会或个人用来衡量某物价值的尺度
senses.example: Health has no price in the ordinary market sense.
senses.exampleCN: 健康在普通市场意义上没有价格。
senses.why: the word generalizes once value itself is what is being measured, not only goods.
senses.whyCN: 当被衡量的是价值本身而非仅商品时，这个词就一般化了。

intro.en: Price comes through Old French pris from Latin pretium 'price, value, reward'. It is a doublet of prize in the sense of value, but not of prize meaning an award. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: price 经古法语 pris 上溯拉丁 pretium「价格、价值、报酬」。它与表示「价值」的 prize 是对偶词，但与表示「奖赏」的 prize 不是。年代均为约数。

items.en: Pretium covered price, value and reward, so the Latin word already contained both the commercial and the figurative seeds.
items.cn: pretium 兼指价格、价值与报酬，因此这个拉丁词已同时含商业义与比喻义的种子。

items.en: Old French pris meant the amount asked or the worth of a thing, and passed both senses to English.
items.cn: 古法语 pris 指索要的金额或某物的价值，并把这两层意思都传给英语。

items.en: English price appears in the thirteenth century; the plural came to mean the general cost of living.
items.cn: 英语 price 出现于 13 世纪；其复数后来指一般生活成本。

items.en: Prize meaning value is a variant of price; prize meaning an award came from Old French prise 'a capture', from prendre 'to take', a different root.
items.cn: 表示「价值」的 prize 是 price 的变体；表示「奖赏」的 prize 来自古法语 prise「捕获」，再上溯 prendre「拿取」，词根不同。

items.en: The figurative price of success and the betting price of a horse extend the same core: something must be paid for an outcome.
items.cn: 「成功的代价」与赛马的「赔率」都延伸同一核心：为了某个结果必须付出某物。

items.en: The exact first English citation is approximate. Latin pretium and Old French pris are well documented.
items.cn: 最早的英语书证年代只是约数。拉丁 pretium 与古法语 pris 都有充分书证。

note.en: Group one holds words that look like price or share its root but differ in sense; group two holds near terms for an amount charged.
note.cn: 第一组是形似 price 或与其同根、但意义不同的词；第二组是表示「所收金额」的近义词。

entries.definition: As value, it is a doublet of price; as an award, it descends from prendre 'to take'. Only the first sense is etymologically the same word.
entries.definitionCN: 作「价值」解时，它是 price 的对偶词；作「奖赏」解时，上溯 prendre「拿取」。只有前一义在词源上是同一个词。

entries.definition: From Latin pretiosus 'costly', built on pretium; it describes worth, not the amount charged.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 pretiosus「贵重」，建于 pretium 之上；它描述价值，而非所收金额。

entries.definition: From ad- plus pretiare 'to value'; it means to estimate worth, not to set a selling price.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 ad- 加 pretiare「估价」；意为估算价值，而非设定售价。

entries.definition: Built on price with -y, meaning expensive; it describes the level, not the amount itself.
entries.definitionCN: 由 price 加 -y 构成，意为昂贵；它描述水平，而非金额本身。

entries.definition: The expense of making or obtaining something; price is what the buyer pays, and the two need not be equal.
entries.definitionCN: 制作或取得某物的支出；price 是买主所付，两者不必相等。

entries.definition: The amount a provider demands for a service; it is close to price but more common for services and fees.
entries.definitionCN: 服务提供者索要的金额；与 price 接近，但更常用于服务与费用。

entries.definition: A fixed payment for a professional service or privilege; it is a kind of price with a narrower setting.
entries.definitionCN: 为专业服务或特权支付的固定款项；它是范围更窄的一类价格。

entries.definition: The worth of something to a person; price is what is asked, while value is what is judged.
entries.definitionCN: 某物对某人的价值；price 是所要之数，value 是被判断的价值。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin pretium 'value': the same root runs through price, precious and appraise.
normal.cn: 拉丁 pretium「价值」：同一词根贯穿 price、precious 与 appraise。

normal.en: The family runs price, pricing, priced, pricey, priceless, overprice, underprice.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 price、pricing、priced、pricey、priceless、overprice、underprice。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the commercial sense: market price, price tag, price increase.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出商业义：市场价格、价签、价格上涨。

normal.en: The figurative sense is marked by of: the price of success, the price of silence.
normal.cn: 比喻义由 of 标出：成功的代价、沉默的代价。

normal.en: Betting uses price for odds, because a stake buys a chance at a return.
normal.cn: 博彩用 price 指赔率，因为赌注买到的是一次回报机会。

abstract.en: Picture a tiny tag that decides whether a hand reaches out or moves on.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚小小的价签，决定一只手是伸出去还是走开。

abstract.en: Picture a coin placed on one side of a scale and a thing on the other.
abstract.cn: 想象天平一边放硬币，另一边放物品。

abstract.en: Picture a finish line with a toll booth in front of it.
abstract.cn: 想象一条终点线前面立着一个收费亭。

examples.en: The price of the ticket includes the ferry crossing.
examples.cn: 票价包含渡船费用。

examples.en: They paid a high price for ignoring the warning.
examples.cn: 他们因忽视警告付出了高昂代价。

examples.en: The dealer quoted a price for the old car.
examples.cn: 经销商为这辆旧车报了价。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「price（价格）」——货架上那个决定买不买的数字 → 价格、代价

root: 拉丁 pretium「价格、价值、报酬」→ 古法语 pris → 英语 price；与表示「奖赏」的 prize 不同源，但与表示「价值」的 prize 属对偶词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one number: a seller states what a thing costs, and that number is then read as a tag, a sacrifice, a verb, a general level, a reward, a quoted rate, betting odds, and finally any scale of worth.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个数字展开：卖方说出某物要多少钱，这个数字再被读作价签、牺牲、动词、总体水平、赏金、报价、赔率，最后是任何价值尺度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one small tag whose number decides whether a hand reaches out.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚小价签，其数字决定一只手是否伸出。

branches.en: AMOUNT AND ACT: the number on the tag, and the act of putting it there.
branches.cn: 金额与动作：价签上的数字，以及把数字放上去的动作。

branches.en: SACRIFICE AND SCALE: what must be given up, and the wider measure of worth it implies.
branches.cn: 牺牲与尺度：必须放弃的东西，以及它所含的更广价值尺度。

branches.en: THE GENERAL LEVEL: prices in the plural become the cost of living.
branches.cn: 总体水平：复数的 prices 成为生活成本。

branches.en: REWARD AND QUOTE: a sum offered for a capture, and a rate quoted in a market.
branches.cn: 赏金与报价：为缉拿所设的金额，以及市场中报出的价位。

branches.en: BETTING ODDS: the stake buys a chance, so the odds are called a price.
branches.cn: 博彩赔率：赌注买到机会，因此赔率被称作价格。

intro.en: Price is a borrowed Latin noun that English has turned into a verb, an adjective and an action noun, so the family spreads in several directions.
intro.cn: price 是借入的拉丁名词，英语把它变成动词、形容词与动作名词，因此词族向多个方向展开。

latinIntro.en: Latin pretium, pretiosus and pretiare supply price, precious, appraise and appreciate; English suffixes supply pricing, priced, pricey and priceless.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 pretium、pretiosus 与 pretiare 提供 price、precious、appraise 与 appreciate；英语后缀提供 pricing、priced、pricey 与 priceless。

items.example: The root carries both money and worth.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根兼含金钱与价值。

items.structure: Latin pretium via Old French pris
items.example: The price held steady all year.
The book is priced at twelve pounds.
The seats were pricey but comfortable.
The diary is priceless to historians.
items.exampleCN: 这本日记对历史学者而言无价。
卖方把这套房子定价过高。

items.example: They underpriced the tickets and sold out.
items.exampleCN: 他们把票价定得过低，结果售罄。
一位估价师为这幅画估了价。

latinEntries.meaning: to value, set a price on

definition_zh: 自豪；骄傲；傲慢；自尊（心）；狮群；以……为荣
definition_en: a warm feeling about one's own or another's achievement; an excessive sense of one's own importance; self-respect; a group of lions; and, as a verb, to feel proud about something one has
core_image: 胸膛往上一提，下巴微微抬起的那一瞬
scene: 毕业典礼上，主持人念到儿子的名字，母亲坐在观众席里，背一下子挺直了。Her face shone with pride as her son walked across the stage to take his diploma.
sceneCN: 这里 pride 指「自豪、骄傲」（第 1 个义项：因自己或亲近的人取得成绩而心里发亮）；句意为儿子走上台领取毕业证书时，她脸上泛着自豪的光。图中可辨识物件：毕业证书、观众席、被念到名字的学生。

pos.zh: 自豪；骄傲；傲慢；自尊；狮群
以……为荣（用于 pride oneself on）

derivatives.zh: 与 pride 同属古英语 prūd 词族，但不是由 pride 加后缀得来：pride 是名词，proud 是形容词，义为「自豪的；骄傲的」
由 pride 加形容词后缀 -ful 构成，义为「自负的；傲慢的」
由形容词 proud 加 -ly 构成，义为「自豪地；得意地」，与 pride 同源而词形不同

senses.title: A warm feeling about one's own or another's success
senses.definition: a feeling of deep pleasure and satisfaction that comes from what you or people close to you have done or possess
senses.definitionCN: 因自己或亲近的人所做成、所拥有的事而感到的深切愉快与满足
senses.example: She looked at her finished painting with quiet pride.
senses.exampleCN: 她带着平静的自豪看着自己画完的画。
senses.why: The Old English noun first named the bare quality of being proud, and English kept its warmer half: the lift a person feels when something of theirs turns out well.
senses.whyCN: 古英语名词最早只指「骄傲」这种性质，英语留下了它温暖的一半：当自己这边的事情做成了，人心里往上一提，这就是自豪。

senses.title: An exaggerated belief in one's own importance
senses.definition: an unreasonable feeling that you are better or more important than other people
senses.definitionCN: 毫无道理地觉得自己比别人强、比别人重要
senses.example: It was pride, not principle, that stopped him from admitting the mistake.
senses.exampleCN: 让他不肯认错的是自大，而不是原则。
senses.why: The same self-regard that lifts a person up can also close the ears: once the good opinion of oneself grows past what the facts support, the word slides into the vice that preachers warn against.
senses.whyCN: 同一种自我看重既能让人挺起胸，也能堵住耳朵：当一个人对自己的好评超过了事实能撑住的分量，这个词就滑向传道者所警告的那种恶。

senses.title: The respect a person keeps for themselves
senses.definition: a proper sense of one's own worth that keeps a person from doing something shameful
senses.definitionCN: 对自己价值的正当意识，使人不肯做出丢脸的事
senses.example: He had too much pride to ask for help with the rent.
senses.exampleCN: 他的自尊心太强，不肯开口求人帮忙付房租。
senses.why: Between the warm sense and the arrogant one lies a third: pride as the floor a person refuses to sink below, the line kept even when nobody is watching.
senses.whyCN: 在「暖」和「傲」之间还有第三层：pride 是一个人拒绝再往下退的那块地板，即使没人看着也不肯越过的界线，所以是自尊。

senses.title: A group of lions living and hunting together
senses.definition: a group of lions that live and hunt together, usually led by related females
senses.definitionCN: 共同生活、共同捕猎的一群狮子，通常由有亲缘关系的母狮带领
senses.example: A pride of lions lay in the shade, waiting for the heat to pass.
senses.exampleCN: 一群狮子卧在树荫里，等暑气过去。
senses.why: This sense comes from medieval hunting language, where each kind of animal was given its own company name; naming a band of lions was one entry in that list, and only this one survived in everyday use.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项来自中世纪的狩猎用语，当时人们给每一种动物的群体都起一个专门的集合名，狮子那一栏就是 pride，而这一栏是唯一留到日常英语里的。

senses.title: To feel proud about a skill or possession of one's own
senses.definition: to feel a strong, often slightly self-satisfied pleasure about a skill, quality, or possession of one's own
senses.definitionCN: 对自己拥有的本领、品质或东西感到强烈的、常带点自得的满意
senses.example: The old chef prides himself on never using a shortcut.
senses.exampleCN: 这位老厨师最得意的是自己从不走捷径。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb inside the pattern to pride oneself on, where oneself is the person being lifted and the preposition on names the thing that does the lifting.
senses.whyCN: 名词套进 to pride oneself on 这个句式后就当动词用：oneself 是被抬起来的那个自己，介词 on 后面则是抬人的理由，也就是凭什么觉得自己了不起。

intro.en: Pride is an Old English noun built on the adjective proud, and that adjective is generally traced through French to a Late Latin word for profit; the word therefore began as a judgement of worth before it split into warm and cold senses.
intro.cn: pride 是古英语里由形容词 proud 造出的名词，而那个形容词一般认为经法语上溯到晚期拉丁语中表示「有好处」的词；所以它最初是对「有没有价值」的判断，之后才分成暖、冷两路。

items.en: The Latin verb prodesse meant to be of use or of advantage, and its stem prōd- is the base that later Romance forms are usually traced to.
items.cn: 拉丁语动词 prodesse 意为「有用、有好处」，一般认为后来的罗曼语词形都追到它的词干 prōd-。

items.en: The Late Latin form prode meant useful or profitable, and in the spoken Latin of the provinces it also took on the colour of brave or worthy.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语的 prode 意为「有用的、有利的」，在各省的口语拉丁语里又沾上了「勇敢、可敬」的色彩。

items.en: Old French prud or prod described a man who was brave and worthy, a sense still visible in the modern French preux.
items.cn: 古法语 prud、prod 形容人勇敢可敬，这层意思在今天的法语 preux 里还能看到。

items.en: English borrowed the adjective as prūd, which in Old English already meant proud, arrogant, and splendid at the same time; from it the noun prȳde was formed.
items.cn: 英语借入这个形容词，写作古英语 prūd，当时就同时表示「骄傲的、傲慢的、华贵的」三面；名词 prȳde 正是由它造出来的。

items.en: Middle English prede or pride settled on the spelling pride, and the old single quality divided into praise-worthy self-respect and blame-worthy conceit, with the lion sense added from hunting vocabulary.
items.cn: 中古英语的 prede、pride 最终定为 pride 这个拼写，原本混在一起的性质分成值得称赞的自尊与该受责备的自负，狮群一义则从狩猎词汇补进来。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the adjective that pride was built from and the words closest to it in spelling; the near-meaning group holds words for self-regard, both deserved and inflated.
note.cn: 形近组收了 pride 借以构成的那个形容词及拼写最接近的几个词；近义组收表示自我看重的词，既有应得的，也有膨胀的。

entries.definition: Feeling pleased about one's own or another's achievements; the adjective that English used to build the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 为自己或他人的成就感到高兴的；英语正是用它造出了名词 pride。

entries.definition: Showing too high an opinion of oneself; built on the noun with the suffix -ful.
entries.definitionCN: 过于自负的；由名词加后缀 -ful 构成。

entries.definition: A person who is easily shocked by matters of the body; it comes from a French word for a modest woman, so the similarity is only in spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 对身体方面的事容易大惊小怪的人；来自法语中表示「端庄女子」的词，只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: To push someone or something with a finger or a stick; a different word with a different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 用手指或棍子捅；另一个词，来源不同。

entries.definition: An unpleasant belief that one is better than everyone else.
entries.definitionCN: 令人反感的、认为自己高于所有人的信念。

entries.definition: The calm, serious quality of deserving respect.
entries.definitionCN: 值得尊重的沉稳庄重。

entries.definition: The good opinion a person has of their own character.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人对自身品格的正面评价。

entries.definition: The pleasant feeling of having got what one wanted.
entries.definitionCN: 得到想要之物后的愉快感觉。

normalIntro.en: The noun was grown from an adjective that English borrowed from French, so the family keeps one ancient stem but two different shapes.
normalIntro.cn: 这个名词是从英语借自法语的形容词上长出来的，所以同族词共用一个古老词干，却有两种不同词形。

normal.en: Pride is the noun and proud is the adjective: English formed prȳde from prūd, which is why the two never look alike today.
normal.cn: pride 是名词，proud 是形容词：古英语从 prūd 造出 prȳde，所以今天两者词形完全不同。

normal.en: The -ful in prideful turns the noun into an adjective, the same -ful that appears in careful and hopeful.
normal.cn: prideful 里的 -ful 把名词变成形容词，和 careful、hopeful 里的 -ful 是同一个后缀。

normal.en: Swallow one's pride is a picture of forcing something down the throat: the feeling is still there, only hidden.
normal.cn: swallow one's pride 是一幅把东西硬咽下去的画：情绪还在，只是藏起来了。

normal.en: A pride of lions follows the old hunting habit of giving every kind of animal its own collective name.
normal.cn: a pride of lions 沿用古老的狩猎习惯：给每一种动物的群体都起一个专门的集合名。

normal.en: Pride oneself on needs the reflexive pronoun because the one who boasts is also the one being lifted.
normal.cn: pride oneself on 必须带反身代词，因为夸人的和被抬高的其实是同一个。

abstract.en: One word covers a mother's lifted chin and a tyrant's closed ears, because both are the same self looking at itself.
abstract.cn: 一个词同时装着母亲抬起的下巴和暴君堵住的耳朵，因为两者都是「自我在看自己」。

abstract.en: Pride as dignity is pride turned inward and kept quiet; pride as conceit is the same force turned outward and made loud.
abstract.cn: 作为尊严的 pride 向内收着、不出声；作为自负的 pride 是同一股力向外放、喊得很响。

abstract.en: The lion sense survives as a fossil: a whole medieval habit of naming animal groups, kept alive by one entry.
abstract.cn: 狮群义像一块化石：中世纪给动物群体起名的一整套习惯，只靠这一条留了下来。

examples.en: She looked at her finished painting with quiet pride.
examples.cn: 她带着平静的自豪看着自己画完的画。

examples.en: It was pride, not principle, that stopped him from admitting the mistake.
examples.cn: 让他不肯认错的是自大，而不是原则。

examples.en: The old chef prides himself on never using a shortcut.
examples.cn: 这位老厨师最得意的是自己从不走捷径。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「扑赖德」——一股气从胸口扑上来，赖着不走，那就是 pride。

root: 古英语 prȳde（骄傲）由 prūd（骄傲的）加名词词尾构成，prūd 一般认为借自古法语 prud、prod，可上溯到晚期拉丁语 prode（有用的、有利的），出自拉丁语 prodesse（有益）。同源的形容词 proud 保留了另一支词形。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a self looking at itself with approval; the senses divide into the warm feeling, the cold excess, the line of self-respect, the lion group, and the verb of taking pride in something.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「自我满意地看着自己」；义项由此分出温暖的自豪、过头的自负、守住的尊严、狮群，以及表示「以……为荣」的动词用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chest lifting and a chin rising for a moment.
core.cn: 核心意象：胸口往上一提，下巴微微一抬的那一瞬。

branches.en: a mother's back straightening at a ceremony
branches.cn: 典礼上母亲把背挺直的一瞬

branches.en: a man who will not say sorry
branches.cn: 一个死活不肯道歉的人

branches.en: a hand pushing away a coin offered in pity
branches.cn: 一只推开怜悯施舍的手

branches.en: tawny bodies resting in tall grass
branches.cn: 高草里卧着的一群黄褐色身影
